title: perf: log-mel FFT twiddle precompute + alloc-elimination (mel frontend)
description: whisper.cpp's recursive fft (src/native_engine/mel.rs) recomputes cos/sin twiddles per butterfly per frame; the odd-N base case dft(25) is reached 16x/frame x 3000 frames, ~60M f64 transcendentals per 30s audio. L1 (this turn): precompute level + DFT twiddle tables once (cached OnceLock, shared across mel worker threads), bit-exact (same f64 math + as-f32 narrowing at build time). Guarded by fft_twiddle_table_is_bit_exact_vs_inline_reference (10 widths x 64 seeds). L2 (follow-up): eliminate the per-call Vec allocations in the recursive fft (even/odd/even_fft/odd_fft, ~60 allocs/frame) via per-thread scratch buffers. Measured head-to-head via native_engine/mel/mel_30s vs mel-pre baseline (269ms).
notes: L1 LANDED in commit 656f55c (origin/main + master): log-mel FFT twiddle precompute. Measured native_engine/mel/mel_30s 269.06ms -> 29.23ms (-89.1%, p=0.00, ~9.2x) same-worker A/B on vmi1149989. Bit-exact: standalone parity 418800 outputs / 0 mismatches + in-tree test fft_twiddle_table_is_bit_exact_vs_inline_reference. L2 (per-call alloc elimination in recursive fft via per-thread scratch) remains open as follow-up. Ledger: docs/PERF_LEDGER.md.
close_reason: L1 shipped (9.2x mel); L2 measured (1.21x FFT, ~0 e2e) and deferred per revert-~0-gain.

title: Build original-vs-franken benchmark ledger harness
description:
## Background
The mission is to dominate the original OpenAI Whisper / whisper.cpp stack on realistic workloads, but current artifacts mix true original-vs-franken proof with internal franken policy comparisons. This bead establishes the head-to-head measurement substrate and makes docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md the claim ledger.

## Scope
Create a reproducible per-crate benchmark/evidence harness that records every original-vs-franken win, loss, neutral result, and reverted candidate. The harness must run only this crate, with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/franken_whisper-cod-a` and `rch exec -- cargo bench --release ...`; never run workspace-wide benches.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparators: `whisper.cpp` / `whisper-cli` CPU for primary CPU claims; optional GPU comparator as a clearly labeled control. OpenAI Whisper Python and related original-stack tools can be added only when the workload needs that comparator.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- `alien_cs_graveyard.md` section 0.10 statistical benchmarking standard.
- `alien_cs_graveyard.md` section 0.19 evidence ledger schema.
- `profiling-software-performance`: fingerprint, p50/p95/p99, RSS, hotspot table.
- `extreme-software-optimization`: one lever, isomorphism proof, re-profile.

## Validation
Artifacts for each run must include env/fingerprint, exact command lines, raw criterion or hyperfine output, p50/p95/p99, RSS/user CPU when available, conformance/golden hashes, and a ledger row in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md or its successor.

## Tests
Run the smallest relevant per-crate Criterion bench through rch after harness changes, plus `cargo fmt --check` if code changes. No claim may be accepted from a single run or from cross-host-only evidence.

## Success Criteria
A future agent can add a new measured claim by following one documented command block and gets a machine-readable ratio row: workload, franken path, original path, speed_ratio, conformance status, artifact path, and verdict.

title: Measure and fix shipped release-profile native speed gap
description:
## Background
Existing artifacts say the distribution `release` profile uses `opt-level = \"z\"` and was about 26% slower than `release-perf` on `large-v3-turbo`. The README headline claims are from `release-perf`, but users run shipped release binaries. If shipped release loses to whisper.cpp while release-perf is at parity, this is the biggest real-world domination gap.

## Scope
Measure native `release`, native `release-perf`, and original `whisper.cpp` CPU on the same host and same audio/model corpus. If the release profile is a confirmed top lever, make one Cargo profile change only, then re-benchmark and update the ledger. Do not combine with native-engine kernel changes.

## Baseline Comparator
Primary: `whisper.cpp` CPU on the same input/model. Controls: native `release-perf`; optional `whisper.cpp` GPU/Metal clearly marked as a hardware-control loss/win, not a CPU claim.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard section 0.10: statistical benchmark acceptance, p50/p95/p99 and confidence interval discipline.
- Extreme optimization: one profile lever per commit; prove behavior unchanged via golden transcripts and conformance hashes.
- Artifact coding: policy decision is not adaptive; fallback is reverting the Cargo profile if binary size or wall time fails budget.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: bigger binaries or slower cold builds. Budgeted mode: record binary size, build time, wall, user CPU, and conformance. Fallback trigger: less than 3% wall win vs current release or unacceptable binary-size growth per release owner policy.

## Validation
Run per-crate through rch only, with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/data/projects/.rch-targets/franken_whisper-cod-a`. Required gates: original-vs-franken ratio row, golden transcript hash match, conformance green, and no new negative-evidence collision.

## Success Criteria
Shipped release binary is at least parity with current release-perf against whisper.cpp CPU on `tiny.en` and `large-v3-turbo`, or the bead closes as negative evidence with exact ratio and reason.
close_reason: Completed: release profile opt-level=3 is already landed on main in 866760c with docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md release-profile ratio evidence; current Cargo.toml keeps [profile.release] opt-level=3.

title: Foundation: Legacy Analysis, Project Infrastructure, and Porting Strategy
description:
EPIC: Foundation & Legacy Analysis

This epic covers the foundational work that ALL other work depends on. franken_whisper is a Rust-native ASR system that merges the best IDEAS (not code) from three legacy projects into something radically better:

- legacy_whispercpp (C/C++): Fast local inference, VAD (Silero), streaming, multi-platform HW accel, TinyDiarize, word-level timestamps, quantized models, 60+ CLI flags
- legacy_insanely_fast_whisper (Python): Flash Attention 2 (15x speedup), GPU batching, ergonomic CLI, pyannote diarization
- legacy_whisper_diarization (Python): Multi-stage pipeline (Demucs source separation → Faster-Whisper → CTC forced alignment → NeMo TitaNet speaker embeddings → multilingual punctuation restoration)

The merger pattern follows frankentui's proven methodology: SYNTHESIS not merger, CONCEPTS not copy-paste, DESIGN-DRIVEN not code-driven. The frankentui project demonstrated that planning before code (the first 48 hours were ALL planning) produces dramatically better results.

This project must deeply integrate with:
- asupersync: Cancel-correct async orchestration (not just Runtime::new — use Cx, regions, finalizers, budgets)
- frankensqlite: MVCC concurrent writes + RaptorQ durability (not just basic open/execute)
- frankentorch: GPU tensor operations + autograd (for acceleration beyond simple softmax)
- frankenjax: JIT-compiled transform graphs (for declarative computation paths)
- frankentui: Optional TUI for human operators

The project is BOTH a reusable Rust library AND a standalone CLI with robot mode (agent-first NDJSON) + optional TUI.

Key constraints: #![forbid(unsafe_code)], Rust 2024 edition, nightly toolchain, Cargo only, fsqlite only (no rusqlite).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All three legacy projects (whisper.cpp, insanely-fast-whisper, whisper-diarization) analyzed with strengths/weaknesses documented
- Cargo.toml validates with correct edition, features, dependencies
- All quality gates pass (fmt, check, clippy, test)
- FEATURE_PARITY.md tracks every legacy feature with migration status
- PROPOSED_ARCHITECTURE.md reflects deep integration plan
- Porting strategy document is self-contained and actionable.
acceptance_criteria: - All three legacy projects (whisper.cpp, insanely-fast-whisper, whisper-diarization) analyzed with strengths/weaknesses documented. - Cargo.toml validates with correct edition, features, dependencies. - All quality gates pass (fmt, check, clippy, test). - FEATURE_PARITY.md tracks every legacy feature with migration status. - PROPOSED_ARCHITECTURE.md reflects deep integration plan. - Porting strategy document is self-contained and actionable.

title: Document legacy project analysis: what each project excels at
description:
Create a comprehensive analysis document (or update EXISTING_LEGACY_WHISPER_STRUCTURE.md) that catalogs:

FROM legacy_whispercpp (C/C++):
- Fast local inference via ggml (no ML framework dependency)
- Silero-VAD integration for speech pre-filtering
- Real-time streaming transcription (whisper-stream binary)
- Multi-platform HW acceleration: ARM NEON, AVX/AVX2, Metal, Core ML, CUDA/cuBLAS, Vulkan, OpenVINO
- TinyDiarize for lightweight speaker turn detection
- Word-level timestamps via -ml 1 flag
- Integer quantization (Q5_0 etc.) for model compression
- Multiple output formats: JSON, VTT, SRT, LRC, CSV, karaoke video
- HTTP server with multipart file uploads
- Confidence color-coding for terminal output
- Performance benchmarking tool (whisper-bench)

FROM legacy_insanely_fast_whisper (Python/Transformers):
- Flash Attention 2 support (15x speedup on long audio)
- GPU batching with configurable batch_size (default 24)
- BetterTransformer integration
- FP16 mixed precision
- Distil-whisper support for smaller model footprint
- Clean ergonomic CLI design (simple, opinionated)
- Direct URL input support (download and transcribe)
- Rich progress indicators
- pyannote.audio v3.1 diarization integration with HF token
- Speaker count control (num/min/max speakers)
- Word-level and chunk-level timestamp options

FROM legacy_whisper_diarization (Python/Faster-Whisper/NeMo):
- Multi-stage pipeline architecture:
  1. Demucs source separation (isolate vocals)
  2. Faster-Whisper ASR
  3. CTC forced alignment (ctc-forced-aligner for timestamp correction)
  4. MarbleNet VAD
  5. TitaNet speaker embedding extraction
  6. Speaker clustering and matching
  7. Multilingual punctuation restoration (12+ languages)
- Word-level speaker attribution (not just segment-level)
- Parallel processing mode (diarize_parallel.py) for >10GB VRAM
- SRT output with speaker labels
- Numeral suppression for alignment accuracy

For each capability, note:
- Whether it's already implemented in franken_whisper
- Whether it should be implemented natively in Rust vs bridged via subprocess
- Priority (essential vs nice-to-have)
- Dependencies on other beads

- Each project has: key features list, architectural pattern summary, performance characteristics, known limitations
- Cross-project comparison matrix exists
- Document is self-contained (no need to read legacy source).

title: native_engine/mel.rs: log-mel frontend (mixed-radix FFT, exact whisper semantics)
description:
Implement src/native_engine/mel.rs: log-mel spectrogram frontend (pure Rust, exact whisper semantics).

SPEC (mirror whisper.cpp log_mel_spectrogram):
- Constants: SAMPLE_RATE 16000, N_FFT 400, HOP 160, CHUNK 30s -> 3000 mel frames per window; n_mel from model (80 or 128).
- Hann window (periodic, length 400): w[i] = 0.5*(1 - cos(2*pi*i/400)).
- Reflective padding of N_FFT/2 on both sides (whisper.cpp pads with reflection); audio windows beyond end zero-padded to full 30s chunk (3000 frames) — match whisper.cpp behavior of padding to chunk.
- FFT: iterative radix-2 complex FFT, length 400 is NOT a power of two — whisper.cpp zero-pads?? NO: whisper.cpp uses a hybrid (dft for non-pow2). DECISION: implement Bluestein or mixed-radix? SIMPLEST CORRECT: real-input DFT length-400 via Goertzel is O(N^2)=160k ops/frame * 3000 frames = 480M flops — too slow in debug but fine in release w/ rayon? Better: radix-2 FFT of length 512 is WRONG (changes bins). Use mixed-radix FFT supporting 400 = 2^4 * 5^2 (radix-2 + radix-5 stages), or Bluestein via pow2 1024. Implement radix-2+radix-5 mixed FFT with tests vs naive DFT (exact within 1e-4). Power spectrum bins 0..=200 (onesided 201).
- Mel projection: filters (n_mel x 201) from ggml file (A1) matmul power spectrum -> mel energies; log10(max(e,1e-10)); dynamic-range clamp: log_spec = max(log_spec, log_spec.max() - 8.0); normalize (log_spec + 4.0)/4.0. EXACTLY as whisper.cpp/openai.
- Parallelize frames with rayon (via ft-kernel-cpu's rayon — or std::thread::scope chunks; keep it simple, frames are independent).
- API: fn log_mel(samples: &[f32], filters: &MelFilterbank, n_threads) -> Mel { n_mel, n_frames, data } and helper to slice/pad a 30s window -> 3000 frames.
TESTS: (1) FFT vs naive DFT on random vectors (sizes 400, 200) rel err < 1e-4; (2) Parseval energy check; (3) golden test: silence -> all frames equal floor value (compute expected analytically); (4) 440Hz sine -> argmax mel bin matches analytic mel bin for 440Hz given the real tiny.en filterbank (gated on model presence); (5) determinism across thread counts.
close_reason: Implemented log-mel frontend in src/native_engine/mel.rs: periodic Hann window, exact whisper.cpp padding (leading reflective N_FFT/2, trailing 30s+N_FFT/2 zeros), recursive radix-2 FFT with naive-DFT odd base case (400->200->100->50->25), power spectrum re^2+im^2, 201-bin mel projection, log10(1e-10) floor, global max-8 clamp, (x+4)/4 normalize. std::thread::scope frame parallelism (no rayon). 6 tests pass incl FFT-vs-naive-DFT (400/256/200/5 <1e-4), Parseval, silence->-1.5 floor, n_threads 1==4 determinism, chunk_frames silence-floor padding, gated 440Hz argmax. clippy/rustfmt clean, no unsafe, no unwrap outside tests.

title: Backend System: Enhanced Multi-Backend Architecture with Streaming
description:
EPIC: Backend System Enhancement

The backend system bridges franken_whisper to three external ASR engines via subprocess invocation. Current implementation is functional but basic — it runs a command, waits for completion, parses output JSON.

Each legacy project excels at different things:
- whisper.cpp: VAD pre-filtering, streaming, word-level timestamps, quantized models, multi-HW accel

1. Streaming results: Instead of waiting for full completion, stream partial transcripts as backends produce them (whisper.cpp already supports this natively)
2. Backend health probing: Cache availability checks, detect GPU/CPU capability, report diagnostics
3. Configuration profiles: Allow tuning per-backend parameters (batch size, model, device, precision)
4. Output format normalization: Unified segment model regardless of which backend produced it
5. Multi-backend consensus: Run multiple backends, compare results, pick best (alien-artifact two-lane execution)
6. Backend-specific optimizations: VAD pre-filtering for whisper.cpp, batch size tuning for insanely-fast, etc.

Auto-selection policy (currently):
- Non-diarization: whisper_cpp → insanely_fast → whisper_diarization
- Diarization: insanely_fast → whisper_diarization → whisper_cpp

Future: Adaptive selection based on input characteristics (duration, noise level, speaker count estimate).

title: Design streaming backend trait for real-time result delivery

title: Implement backend health probing and capability reporting
description:
Before selecting a backend, probe what each can do. Currently we just check if the binary exists.

Comprehensive health probing:
1. BINARY AVAILABILITY: Does binary exist? What version? (whisper-cli --version, etc.)
2. MODEL AVAILABILITY: What models are downloaded? Check model directories/HF cache.
3. GPU CAPABILITY: CUDA, Metal, Vulkan? Available VRAM?
4. FEATURE SUPPORT: VAD? Flash Attention 2? Source separation?

Cache probe results (5-minute TTL) to avoid re-probing every run.

Expose via: robot backends command, CLI backends command, TUI header.

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_probe_binary_exists: Mock which() → backend reported as available
- test_probe_binary_missing: Mock which() fails → backend reported as unavailable with reason
- test_probe_version_parsed: Mock version output → version string extracted correctly
- test_probe_cache_ttl: Probe, wait, probe again → cache hit within TTL, miss after TTL
- test_probe_all_backends: Probe all three backends → aggregated report with correct structure
- test_probe_gpu_detection: Mock GPU detection → capabilities reported correctly
- test_probe_partial_failure: One backend probe fails → others still reported, error noted

LOGGING:
- "Probing backend {name}: binary={path}, version={ver}" at DEBUG
- "Backend {name} unavailable: {reason}" at WARN
- "Using cached probe result for {name} (age={age_secs}s)" at TRACE

## Acceptance Criteria
- When --diarize is set, insanely_fast requires FRANKEN_WHISPER_HF_TOKEN or HF_TOKEN
- Missing token produces clear error message with setup instructions
- Token validation happens before backend execution (fail fast)
- Non-diarization runs do not require token
- Unit test: missing token with --diarize returns DiarizationTokenMissing error
- Unit test: token present allows backend to proceed.

title: Implement unified output format normalization across all backends
description:
Each backend produces different JSON structures. Create robust normalization:

whisper_cpp: {"transcription": [{"timestamps": {...}, "text": "..."}]}
insanely_fast: {"text": "...", "chunks": [{"text": "...", "timestamp": [start, end]}]}
whisper_diarization: .srt with [Speaker N]: prefixes, .txt with plain text

Canonical output: TranscriptionSegment {start_sec, end_sec, text, speaker, confidence}

The normalization layer:
1. Per-backend parsers with comprehensive tests
2. Handle missing fields gracefully
3. Normalize speaker labels (SPEAKER_00 → Speaker 0)
4. Normalize timestamps to seconds
5. Validate output (no overlapping, no negative timestamps)
6. Log warnings for unexpected formats without failing

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_parse_whisper_cpp_standard: Golden JSON → correct segments
- test_parse_whisper_cpp_with_diarize: JSON with [SPEAKER_TURN] → speaker extracted
- test_parse_insanely_fast_standard: Golden JSON → correct segments
- test_parse_insanely_fast_with_speakers: Speaker array → speaker labels mapped
- test_parse_diarization_srt: Golden SRT → correct segments with speakers
- test_parse_diarization_txt_fallback: No SRT, only TXT → single segment with full text
- test_missing_timestamps: JSON without timestamps → None timestamps, no crash
- test_missing_confidence: JSON without confidence → None confidence, no crash
- test_speaker_normalization: SPEAKER_00, Speaker 0, speaker0 → all normalize to "Speaker 0"
- test_timestamp_normalization: HH:MM:SS.mmm → seconds, milliseconds → seconds, seconds → seconds
- test_malformed_json: Truncated/invalid JSON → descriptive error, not panic
- test_empty_segments: Backend returns zero segments → empty vec, warning logged
- All tests use golden files from tests/fixtures/golden/

LOGGING:
- "Parsing {backend} output: {file_path}, {file_size} bytes" at DEBUG
- "Extracted {n} segments from {backend}" at INFO
- "Warning: unexpected field {field} in {backend} output" at WARN

## Acceptance Criteria
- Auto backend selection considers: availability, capability (diarize support), historical performance
- Fallback chain respects priority order from README (non-diarize: whisper_cpp > insanely_fast > whisper_diarization)
- Shadow mode emits routing evidence as stage event
- Unit test: unavailable primary backend falls through to secondary
- Unit test: diarize mode prefers insanely_fast
- Routing decision logged at INFO level.

title: Speculation controller: add runtime double-fold toggle so the Brier-reuse A/B has a faithful historical arm
description: Prerequisite for a bankable verdict on bd-7rxo. The existing pipeline_bench historical arm times recommend() plus apply(), but apply() already contains the one-fold candidate. That baseline performs two folds plus two decision bodies, while the true historical apply() performed two folds plus one decision body, so the 1.186-1.193x result from 60/63 wins is an upper bound rather than an estimate. Add a runtime setter that forces the historical double Brier fold inside apply() itself, mirroring the existing runtime perf toggles; an environment OnceLock cannot switch arms inside one binary. Both arms must then call the real apply() and preserve exact action, fallback, and serialized evidence. The harness must self-report its ELF SHA-256, run order-interleaved A/A before A/B in the same invocation, and decide only on the candidate median against the A/A bootstrap 95% CI with the campaign margin. Report CV as provenance only. The three contended 7.06%, 8.07%, and 8.74% runs show that the old CV threshold was invalid for those runs; they do not prove that a quiet run can never fall below 5%.

title: Robot Mode: Agent-First NDJSON Interface Enhancement
description:
EPIC: Robot Mode Enhancement

Robot mode is the agent-first interface — line-oriented NDJSON events streamed in real-time. This is how other programs (AI agents, automation scripts, CI/CD) interact with franken_whisper. It MUST be:
- Stable schema (versioned, backward-compatible)
- Deterministic where possible
- Explicit error codes (enumerated, documented)
- Line-oriented (jsonl/ndjson)
- Easy to pipe into other tools

Current implementation is functional but can be enhanced:
1. Schema versioning: Include schema_version in every event so consumers can adapt
2. Error code enumeration: Replace ad-hoc error strings with structured codes
3. Progress estimation: Include estimated_progress_pct in stage events
4. Streaming partial transcripts: Emit partial transcript text as segments are produced (not just at completion)
5. Backend availability query: `robot backends` command to list available backends with capabilities
6. Run comparison: `robot diff <run1> <run2>` to compare transcription results
7. Health check: `robot health` to verify system readiness
8. Input validation: `robot validate --input <file>` to check input before committing to a run

The event schema should be documented as a JSON Schema artifact that can be consumed by typed language generators.

Key files: src/robot.rs (112 lines), src/main.rs (robot command handling)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Robot mode outputs stable, versioned NDJSON schema
- All events have explicit error codes
- Schema versioning supports backward compatibility
- Event ordering is guaranteed monotonic
- All robot mode contract tests pass.

title: JSONL Sync: Enhanced Export/Import with Incremental Sync
description:
EPIC: JSONL Sync Enhancement

The JSONL sync system provides one-way export/import between SQLite and JSONL files. This serves auditability (git-friendly), backup, and cross-device transfer.

Current implementation (~900 lines) includes:
- Atomic export with manifest (schema version, timestamps, row counts, SHA256 checksums)
- Import with conflict policies (reject or overwrite)
- File-based locking (PID + timestamp, 5-minute stale detection)
- Sync conflict logging

Enhancement goals:
1. Incremental export: Only export records changed since last export (using updated_at timestamps or WAL position)
2. Selective export: Export specific runs, date ranges, or backends
3. Cross-device merge protocol: More sophisticated conflict resolution (3-way merge using common ancestor)
4. Compression: gzip/zstd compressed JSONL for large datasets
5. Streaming import: Process JSONL line-by-line instead of loading entire file
6. Sync telemetry: Report sync statistics (rows synced, conflicts, duration) as robot events
7. JSONL validation: `sync validate` command to verify JSONL integrity without importing

The sync system follows the project's SQLite+JSONL contract: SQLite is source of truth, JSONL is for auditability and recovery. One-way sync at a time, locked and atomic.

Key files: src/sync.rs (~900 lines)
Related docs: SYNC_STRATEGY.md, RECOVERY_RUNBOOK.md

## Acceptance Criteria
- JSONL export produces complete, checksummed snapshots
- JSONL import handles all conflict policies (reject, skip, overwrite)
- Locking prevents concurrent export/import corruption
- Round-trip: export then import produces identical DB state
- All sync tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: JSONL export produces complete, checksummed snapshots. JSONL import handles all conflict policies (reject, skip, overwrite). Locking prevents concurrent export/import corruption. Round-trip: export then import produces identical DB state. All sync tests pass.

title: EPIC: YouTube ingestion pipeline (yt-dlp orchestration -> native transcription -> md+json)
description:
GOAL: `franken_whisper youtube` — ingest YouTube video URLs (repeated --url), a batch file (one URL/line, #-comments), or playlist URLs; download audio via yt-dlp (orchestrated external tool, probed like whisper-cli/ffmpeg); transcribe with the native engine; emit per-video markdown (call-transcript style: title header, metadata block, timestamped paragraphs with youtu.be deep links, SPEAKER_NN when diarized) + JSON (video metadata + per-utterance records with confidence/window stats).

DESIGN (settled 2026-06-06 from /tmp archaeology of yt-dlp + bulk_youtube_transcript_optimizer):
- yt-dlp CLI contract (integration cheat-sheet, agent-verified): expand = `--flat-playlist --dump-json`; metadata = `-j --no-simulate`; download = `-f ba --no-playlist -o TEMPLATE --print after_move:filepath` + politeness `--sleep-interval 2 --max-sleep-interval 5 --retries 10`; batch = read file ourselves (we need per-URL state, not yt-dlp's batch mode); exit codes 0/1/2/101; probe `--version`, warn if >90 days old. Download bestaudio AS-IS (no -x re-encode) — franken_whisper's own normalize stage handles 16k mono.
- Naming: dual-filename convention (optimizer harvest): sanitized `{upload_date} - {title} [{id}]` base, video id as stable suffix; ASCII-safe sanitizer, length-trimmed; original title preserved in JSON.
- Layout: <out_dir>/audio/<base>.<ext>, <out_dir>/<base>.md, <out_dir>/<base>.json, <out_dir>/.fw_youtube_manifest.json (per-video state machine: pending|expanding|downloading|transcribing|rendering|done|failed{error} — idempotent resume: done videos skipped, failed retried unless --no-retry).
- Concurrency (asupersync-native, cancel-correct): multi-thread RuntimeBuilder; one parent scope; downloads bounded by asupersync semaphore (default 3); transcription SEQUENTIAL (engine saturates cores; long videos route via the contiguous-range insanely-fast scheduling internally anyway); downloads pipeline ahead of transcription via a bounded channel(2); cx.checkpoint() in every loop; Ctrl-C (existing ctrlc handler) cancels: kills yt-dlp children (process-group via existing run_command_cancellable pattern), aborts in-flight transcription via CancellationToken, marks manifest states honestly, exits 130.
- Transcription: library path (NativeWhisperModel/transcribe_samples equivalents via the existing backend dispatch with rollout env honored — reuse backend::execute like the speculative path does, so bridge/native routing + raw_output stay uniform).
- Markdown: H1 = title; metadata table (channel, upload date, duration, URL, video id, model+engine, transcribed timestamp, RTF); body = segments grouped into paragraphs (gap>2.5s or speaker change = new paragraph), each paragraph led by a deep-linked timestamp [m:ss](https://youtu.be/<id>?t=<s>); diarized speakers as **SPEAKER_NN:** prefixes.
- JSON: {video:{id,title,channel,uploader,upload_date,duration,webpage_url,description?}, run:{model,engine,backend,version_tag,started,wall_ms,rtf}, utterances:[{i,start_sec,end_sec,text,confidence,speaker?}], windows:[stats]}.
- Tests: hermetic via a STUB yt-dlp (test fixture shell script emitting canned --dump-json lines + copying a fixture wav as the "download") wired by FRANKEN_WHISPER_YTDLP_BIN override; one #[ignore] real-network smoke. NO network in default tests.

title: youtube: robot-mode NDJSON per-video events
description:
The `youtube` subcommand currently emits only a human one-line summary (or a single final JSON blob with `--json-summary`). The rest of franken_whisper exposes a robot interface (`robot run`, etc.) that streams sequenced, timestamped NDJSON stage events on schema `1.0.0`. The youtube path should offer a matching robot sub-mode that streams per-video stage events instead of a single terminal summary.

Proposed contract (NDJSON, one object per line, stable schema):
- `youtube.run_start` — request accepted; echoes resolved options (output_dir, concurrency, backend, diarize).
- `youtube.discovered` — per video, once resolution/playlist expansion yields it: {id, title, url, playlist_id?}.
- `youtube.downloading` / `youtube.downloaded` — per video, around the yt-dlp fetch: {id, audio_path?, bytes?}.
- `youtube.transcribing` / `youtube.done` — per video, around transcription: {id, md_path, json_path, wall_ms?, rtf?} on done.
- `youtube.skipped` — per video already `done` in the manifest: {id, reason:"already_done"}.
- `youtube.failed` — per video failure: {id, title, error, attempts}.
- `youtube.run_complete` — terminal aggregate: {done:[], skipped:[], failed:[], cancelled:bool}.

Notes:
- Each event carries `schema_version`, a monotonic `seq`, and an RFC-3339 `ts`, matching the existing robot stage-event envelope.
- Honor cancellation: on Ctrl+C emit `youtube.failed`/no further events and a `youtube.run_complete` with `cancelled:true`.
- Could be surfaced as `franken_whisper robot youtube ...` or a `--robot` flag on `youtube`; pick whichever matches the existing robot-interface convention.
- The current `--json-summary` (single final blob) stays as the lightweight scripting path; this adds the streaming path.

title: BUG: Native acoustic CLI rejects valid DTW projection geometry
description:
## Outcome

Make the real native CLI and robot paths accept every valid canonical DTW word/segment timeline needed for acoustic diarization, while continuing to reject genuinely malformed or contradictory time geometry with stable errors.

## Current evidence

The dependency-light diarizer and projection helpers have extensive passing unit coverage, but at least one native acoustic CLI invocation rejects a DTW-derived projection interval as invalid. This is a product-path blocker: lower-level accuracy evidence cannot establish that users can obtain diarized native output.

The likely fault family is a representation contract mismatch among native decoder WordTiming values, raw_output word_timestamps metadata, build_segments_dtw, and project_diarization_onto_segments. Equal/zero-duration boundaries, segment-versus-word shape ambiguity, or end-time normalization must be diagnosed from typed values. Do not assume the validator is wrong and do not weaken non-overlap/finite/positive-duration invariants globally.

## Work plan

1. Capture a minimal public-safe typed fixture at every boundary: decoder word timing, transcript segment, raw JSON representation, projection unit, and final speaker turn.
2. Write the contract for each representation and one canonical internal ProjectionUnit with explicit provenance, start/end semantics, and validation reason codes.
3. Normalize word and segment shapes into that canonical type exactly once.
4. Define behavior for zero-duration timestamp tokens, equal adjacent boundaries, punctuation-only tokens, end-of-audio clamping, missing words, and floating-point tolerance.
5. Fix the root producer/adapter/consumer mismatch.
6. Exercise library, CLI human output, robot JSON/NDJSON, and persistence/recovery.
7. Preserve privacy: fixtures must be synthetic or public-safe and contain no private transcript text, filenames, or audio-derived identifying data.

## Tests

- Unit tests for finite monotonic word timing, valid adjacency, invalid reversal/overlap, zero/equal duration, final boundary, empty segments, punctuation-only units, and exact error-code mapping.
- Property tests generate monotonic finite timelines and assert normalization either produces invariant-valid units or a documented typed rejection; never panic.
- Regression fixture reproduces the current native acoustic CLI failure before the fix and passes after it.
- E2E native engine -> DTW word timing -> acoustic diarization -> projected segments -> JSON/NDJSON -> SQLite/JSONL replay.
- Deterministic replay and byte/schema equivalence for supported modes.
- Negative tests prove that NaN, infinity, reversed intervals, and true overlaps remain rejected.

## Success criteria

- The minimized original product-path failure is understood and recorded as a specific contract violation.
- All valid generated timelines pass the canonical validator and real CLI/robot e2e.
- Invalid timelines fail with stable structured reason codes.
- No validation is weakened without a documented semantic justification.
- Focused and mandatory repository gates pass, and the evidence artifact identifies decoder/config/schema versions.

## Fallback

If word-level timing cannot be made valid for a particular decode, fall back explicitly to validated segment-level projection with a structured degradation reason. Never silently discard diarization or fabricate word boundaries.
close_reason: Root product-path bug diagnosed, repaired, and proved across all child tasks. Native decoder terminal [t,t] observations are normalized once into positive half-open canonical projection units with stable typed errors, provenance, conservative fallback, and no weakened overlap/finite invariants. Real native acoustic CLI/robot path now succeeds and durable replay preserves the corrected contract. See bd-2noc.1, bd-2noc.2, and bd-2noc.3 for minimized evidence, implementation, and product-surface proof.

title: Diagnose DTW-to-projection shape mismatch with a minimized typed fixture
description:
## Outcome

Produce the smallest public-safe reproduction of the native acoustic CLI projection failure and identify the exact producer/adapter/consumer contract mismatch before changing validation.

## Work

- Trace one failing invocation through native decoder WordTiming, build_segments_dtw, raw_output metadata, diarization turn production, and project_diarization_onto_segments.
- Record typed values and invariants at each boundary using synthetic or public-safe tokens only.
- Classify the failure as producer bug, representation ambiguity, tolerance/quantization issue, adapter bug, or validator bug.
- Add a failing regression test that exercises the actual CLI/robot path, not only a helper.
- Audit adjacent paths for the same shape mismatch: segment timestamps, DTW-disabled decode, empty/punctuation tokens, and persistence replay.

## Success criteria

A deterministic minimized test fails for the original reason, the precise violated contract and owning layer are documented, and no private source content is retained. The task closes with diagnosis and failing proof only; implementation belongs to the dependent repair issue.
notes: Diagnosis complete without production behavior changes. Exact contract mismatch: native DTW grouping can emit zero-width [t,t] words by design after grid quantization; build_segments_dtw copies them unchanged and tags output dtw; generic segment conformance admits zero width; acoustic word projection requires end > start and rejects it. A minimized public-safe typed fixture reproduces adapter acceptance then projection rejection. A gated real native robot run on the existing public JFK fixture proves backend.ok followed by diarize.error and terminal FW-ROBOT-REQUEST. Adjacent audit: non-DTW uses duration-dominance policy; untimed DTW segments already interpolate; punctuation attaches to lexical words; conformance epsilon and projection epsilon also differ; persistence is not reached. Ownership is the adapter normalization boundary, not global validator relaxation. Proof: cargo fmt --check PASS; git diff --check PASS; focused typed test 1/1 PASS; gated robot characterization 1/1 PASS in 17.69s; production/doc UBS PASS. Full changed-file UBS retains 13 pre-existing test-only panic-macro heuristics (same 13 at HEAD) and adds no critical finding. An ovh-b strict-remote retry materialized all sources but failed in num-traits build-script startup with an impossible 648518346341351440-byte allocator request, an infrastructure failure before project compilation.
close_reason: Completed minimized typed and real robot-path diagnosis; adapter normalization is the precise owning layer.

title: Implement one canonical projection-unit normalization and validation contract
description:
## Outcome

Introduce one typed canonical projection unit and normalize every supported decoder/output representation into it exactly once.

## Work

- Specify start/end units, inclusivity, monotonicity, adjacency, duration, end-of-audio clamping, timestamp-token handling, punctuation-only content, and floating tolerance.
- Preserve provenance: word, segment, hint, silence, decoder timestamp, or fallback.
- Separate normalization from invariant validation and provide stable structured error reasons.
- Fix the diagnosed producer/adapter/consumer layer rather than globally relaxing constraints.
- Document the segment-level fallback for unsupported word geometry.

## Tests

Table tests for every representation and edge case; property tests for arbitrary monotonic finite timelines; negative tests for NaN/infinity/reversal/true overlap; deterministic conversion; UBS and mandatory Cargo gates for changed files.

## Success criteria

Every valid input shape maps to the same invariant-valid canonical form, invalid shapes retain strict rejection, the minimized bug passes, and downstream diarization consumes no ambiguous raw shape.
close_reason: Implemented the canonical dtw-projection-v1 normalization boundary: typed positive half-open units, shared 1us adjacency epsilon and 1ms word duration, parent and word fail-closed validation with stable FW-DTW-PROJECTION codes, end-of-parent clamping, zero-width terminal repair, interpolation and geometry fallbacks with exclusive provenance counts, typed word_aligned_safe proof, and alignment-stage preservation of authoritative DTW bytes. Added deterministic table/property/negative tests, raw schema tests, documentation, and a gated real tiny-model robot acoustic diarization pass. Focused projection tests pass 15/15; exact real-model robot e2e passes; fmt and diff checks pass; changed production files have zero UBS critical findings. title: TTY Audio: Low-Bandwidth Audio Relay and Streaming
description:
EPIC: TTY Audio Enhancement

The TTY audio system is a unique innovation — sending audio over terminal PTY/SSH channels where binary streaming is awkward. Current implementation: μ-law encoding + zlib compression + base64 + NDJSON frames.

This is genuinely novel. No legacy project has anything like it. Enhancement goals:
1. Adaptive bitrate: Detect available bandwidth and adjust chunk size/compression
2. Real-time streaming: Currently only file encode/decode; add live mic → NDJSON → remote decode
3. Error correction: Add sequence numbers with gap detection and optional FEC (forward error correction)
4. Pipeline integration: tty-audio input → direct transcription (encode → decode → transcribe in one pipeline)
5. Opus codec option: For higher quality at same bandwidth, offer Opus as alternative to μ-law
6. Bandwidth estimation: Report actual bandwidth usage in robot mode events
7. Two-way relay: Support bidirectional audio for potential voice interaction scenarios

Use case: SSH into a remote server, speak into local mic, have remote franken_whisper transcribe in real-time, stream results back. All over a plain TTY connection.

Key files: src/tty_audio.rs (204 lines)
Codec chain: Input → ffmpeg → 8kHz mono μ-law → chunk → zlib → base64 → NDJSON

## Acceptance Criteria
- TTY audio codec encodes/decodes audio via mu-law + zlib + base64 NDJSON frames
- Round-trip preserves audio quality within acceptable SNR
- Pipeline integration allows TTY-sourced audio to feed into transcription
- Adaptive bitrate adjusts to available bandwidth
- All TTY audio tests pass.

title: Add adaptive bitrate and error correction for TTY audio
description:
Enhance TTY audio for unreliable connections:

1. ADAPTIVE BITRATE: Monitor frame delivery latency. Increase compression if latency rises. Reduce compression when latency is low. Emit bitrate change events as NDJSON.

2. ERROR CORRECTION: Sequence numbers with gap detection (already present). Request retransmit or interpolate on decoder side. Optional FEC using fountain codes (RaptorQ) — same approach frankensqlite uses for WAL self-healing.

3. CONNECTION QUALITY METRICS: Track frame delivery rate, latency p50/p95, loss rate, jitter. Report as NDJSON events periodically. Drive adaptive bitrate decisions.

4. OPUS CODEC OPTION: For higher quality at same bandwidth. Opus at 16kbps significantly outperforms mu-law at 64kbps. Feature-gated behind --codec opus flag.

This is the alien-artifact approach to audio streaming: adaptive, self-healing, measured.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Codec adapts frame size based on measured throughput
- Lower bandwidth reduces frame size (fewer samples per frame)
- Higher bandwidth increases frame size (better compression ratio)
- Adaptation is smooth (no sudden jumps in frame size)
- Unit test: simulated slow pipe triggers smaller frames
- Unit test: simulated fast pipe allows larger frames.

title: Async fsqlite migration broke the build: storage.rs/sync.rs call now-async Connection methods (235 errors)
description:
The frankensqlite async migration (54020c68, a0ab400a; 2026-07-25) turned fsqlite::Connection::{open,query,execute,query_with_params,execute_with_params,execute_with_params_skip_statement_savepoint_in_explicit_txn} into async fn. franken_whisper's storage/sync surface is 100% synchronous and called them directly => 235 compile errors across src/storage.rs and src/sync.rs. The crate did not build at all, blocking every gate, bench and test in the repo (both campaign lanes).

FIX: a BlockingConnection facade in src/storage.rs, following the owner's own precedent for sync harnesses in frankensqlite a0ab400a -- a thread_local asupersync current-thread Runtime + block_on. Facade method names/signatures/error types are identical to the Connection methods they wrap, so ~235 call sites are UNCHANGED. src/sync.rs needed only 'use crate::storage::BlockingConnection as Connection;' plus 18 fully-qualified fsqlite::Connection::open renames -- no signature churn in that 12.8k-line file.

CRITICAL DETAIL: block_on MUST box the future (Box::pin). fsqlite statement futures nest deeply enough that fsqlite raises its own recursion_limit to type-check them; polling one inline overflows the 8 MiB libtest stack. storage::tests::cancel_token_load_latest_expired aborted the suite with SIGABRT (stack overflow) until the box was added.

Also fixed two pre-existing breakages failing the same --all-targets gate: examples/e2e_probe.rs missing the new DecodeParams fields (beam_size/initial_prompt/max_context/suppress_nst), and two AVX2 probe examples violating the workspace unsafe_code=deny lint (allow added, matching how native_engine::nn opts out).

No nesting hazard: RunStore is reachable only from the sync CLI (main.rs, no async fn / no runtime) and its own tests; orchestrator.rs references only FwError::Storage, not the struct.
close_reason: Build restored via BlockingConnection facade (d92b511); release-stack sub-question tracked in PERF_LEDGER + bead comment

Matters because an installed fw binary run outside cargo does not inherit .cargo/config.toml [env]. If release overflows at default stack, the facade needs a dedicated big-stack worker thread owning the runtime (the shape fsqlite's own AsyncConnection uses internally); if it passes, RUST_MIN_STACK is purely dev/test ergonomics.

title: Deep asupersync Integration: Cancel-Correct Orchestration Throughout
description:
EPIC: Deep asupersync Integration

Current state: franken_whisper uses asupersync minimally — just Runtime::new(2 workers, 1 blocking/4 parallelism), spawn, and block_on. This is a "shallow" integration that misses the entire point of asupersync.

Target state: Every pipeline stage flows through Cx capability contexts. Cancellation is a first-class protocol (request → drain → finalize). Resource cleanup is guaranteed via registered finalizers. Bounded cleanup budgets ensure deterministic shutdown times. Lab runtime enables injection testing at every cancellation point.

WHY this matters: The legacy whisper systems have NO cancellation story. A long transcription job that gets cancelled can leave temp files, orphan processes, partial DB writes, and corrupted state. asupersync's cancel-correctness guarantees eliminate this entire class of bugs.

asupersync's four structural guarantees we must leverage:
1. No Orphan Tasks — every spawned task owned by a region; region close waits for ALL children
2. Cancel-Correctness — cancellation as protocol, never silent data loss
3. Bounded Cleanup — cleanup budgets are sufficient conditions, not hopes
4. No Silent Drops — two-phase effects (reserve/commit) prevent data loss

Key integration points:
- Orchestrator pipeline: Each stage (ingest, normalize, backend, accelerate, persist) should be a Cx region
- Backend execution: Subprocess spawning should register finalizers for process cleanup
- Storage: All DB operations should receive &Cx for cancel-safety
- Temp files: Register cleanup finalizers so cancelled runs don't leak disk space
- Robot mode: Event streaming should respect cancellation signals
- TUI: Async event loop should integrate with asupersync runtime

## Acceptance Criteria
- All pipeline stages receive and use Cx capability context.
- Cancellation propagates from root to all child regions within 100ms.
- Finalizers registered for all temp files, subprocesses, and DB transactions.
- Bounded cleanup budgets enforce time limits per stage.
- Lab runtime tests verify cancel-correct behavior.
- Graceful Ctrl+C shutdown works end-to-end.

title: Audit current asupersync usage and identify integration gaps
description:
CURRENT STATE AUDIT:

In src/orchestrator.rs, asupersync is used minimally:
- Runtime::new(RuntimeConfig { worker_threads: 2, blocking_threads: 1, blocking_parallelism: 4 })
- runtime.spawn(async move { run_pipeline(...) })
- runtime.block_on(handle)

This misses almost everything asupersync offers:
- Cx (capability context) is never created or passed
- No regions for stage scoping
- No finalizers for resource cleanup
- No bounded cleanup budgets
- No cancellation injection points
- No two-phase effects (reserve/commit)

The audit should:
1. Read asupersync's API docs and examples (/dp/asupersync/README.md, examples/)
2. Map every place in franken_whisper where Cx should flow
3. Identify all resources that need cleanup finalizers (temp files, subprocesses, DB transactions)
4. Document the integration plan with specific code locations and changes needed

Reference: asupersync's four structural guarantees:
- No Orphan Tasks (region-scoped ownership)
- Cancel-Correctness (request → drain → finalize protocol)
- Bounded Cleanup (time-boxed shutdown)
- No Silent Drops (two-phase effects)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Audit document lists every function that should receive Cx but currently does not.
- Current asupersync usage patterns cataloged (Runtime creation, spawn, region).
- Gap analysis identifies: missing cancellation checks, unregistered cleanup, missing budget enforcement.
- Prioritized list of changes needed per module.

2. For each pipeline stage, create a child region: cx.region("ingest"), cx.region("normalize"), etc.
3. Pass &Cx to: audio::materialize_input(cx, ...), audio::normalize_to_wav(cx, ...), backend::execute(cx, ...), accelerate::run_acceleration(cx, ...), storage::RunStore::persist_report(cx, ...)

title: Register finalizers for temp files, subprocesses, and DB transactions
description:
asupersync's finalizer system ensures resources are cleaned up even when tasks are cancelled. Register finalizers for:

1. TEMP FILES (src/orchestrator.rs): Each run creates a temp directory under .franken_whisper/tmp. Register finalizer to delete on cancellation. Disarm on success.

2. SUBPROCESSES (src/process.rs, src/backend/*.rs): When spawning ffmpeg, whisper-cli, python. Register finalizer to send SIGTERM then SIGKILL after timeout. Prevents zombie processes.

3. DB TRANSACTIONS (src/storage.rs): On BEGIN, register finalizer for ROLLBACK. Disarm on COMMIT.

4. LOCK FILES (src/sync.rs): On lock acquire, register finalizer to release. Prevents stale locks.

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_temp_dir_finalizer: Create temp dir, register finalizer, trigger cancellation → dir deleted
- test_temp_dir_finalizer_disarm: Create temp dir, register finalizer, succeed → dir NOT deleted
- test_subprocess_finalizer: Spawn long-running process, register kill finalizer, cancel → process killed
- test_db_transaction_finalizer: BEGIN, register rollback finalizer, cancel → ROLLBACK executed, no partial data
- test_lock_file_finalizer: Acquire lock, register release finalizer, cancel → lock released
- test_nested_finalizers: Multiple finalizers fire in reverse registration order
- All tests use tracing to log finalizer registration and execution

LOGGING:
- "Registering finalizer for {resource_type}: {description}" at DEBUG
- "Finalizer executed for {resource_type}: {outcome}" at INFO
- "Finalizer disarmed for {resource_type}" at DEBUG

## Acceptance Criteria
- Finalizer registered for every temp file created during pipeline execution.
- Finalizer registered for every subprocess spawned (ffmpeg, whisper-cli, etc).
- Finalizer registered for DB transactions in storage operations.

- Unit test: cancel mid-pipeline verifies temp files cleaned up.
- Unit test: cancel during subprocess verifies process killed.

title: Implement bounded cleanup budgets per pipeline stage
description:
Bounded cleanup ensures that shutdown completes within a known time. Each pipeline stage should have a cleanup budget:

Stage budgets (proposed):
- ingest: 2s (file copy or stdin read should be fast)
- normalize: 5s (ffmpeg may need to flush buffers)
- backend: 10s (external process needs graceful shutdown)
- accelerate: 3s (GPU operations should be bounded)
- persist: 5s (DB transaction commit/rollback)

Total pipeline cleanup budget: 25s maximum

Implementation:
1. Set budget on each region: cx.with_budget(Budget::deadline(Duration::from_secs(10)))
2. If cleanup exceeds budget, escalate (log warning, force-kill)
3. Report actual cleanup times in run events for monitoring

This is especially important for the backend stage — if whisper-cli hangs during cancellation, we need to kill it after the budget expires rather than waiting forever.

The budgets should be configurable (environment variables or config file) for different deployment scenarios (a CI server might want tighter budgets than a desktop workstation).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each pipeline stage has a configurable cleanup budget (default: 5 seconds).
- Budget is enforced: if cleanup exceeds budget, remaining finalizers are skipped with warning.
- Budget inheritance: child regions inherit remaining parent budget.
- Unit test: cleanup budget exceeded triggers warning log.
- Unit test: normal cleanup within budget completes all finalizers.

title: Implement graceful Ctrl+C shutdown via asupersync cancellation protocol
description:
When Ctrl+C (SIGINT) is pressed:
1. Set root cancellation token
2. Allow in-progress stages to drain gracefully
3. Run all registered finalizers (cleanup temp files, kill subprocesses, rollback DB)
4. Emit robot event: {"event": "run_cancelled", "run_id": "...", "stages_completed": [...], "cleanup_summary": {...}}
5. Exit with code 130 (SIGINT convention)

For TUI mode: Restore terminal state before exiting.
For robot mode: Cancelled event is valid NDJSON.

UNIT TESTS REQUIRED (Definition of Done):
- test_sigint_triggers_cancellation: Send SIGINT to child process running pipeline → cancellation propagates
- test_cancelled_event_emitted: After cancellation, verify run_cancelled NDJSON event on stdout
- test_exit_code_130: After SIGINT, exit code is 130
- test_tui_terminal_restored: After SIGINT in TUI mode, terminal is in normal mode (not raw)
- test_cleanup_within_budget: After SIGINT, all cleanup completes within total budget (25s)

LOGGING:
- "SIGINT received, initiating graceful shutdown" at WARN
- "Stage {stage} draining..." at INFO per active stage
- "Cleanup completed in {elapsed_ms}ms" at INFO

title: Deep frankensqlite Integration: MVCC Concurrency and RaptorQ Durability
description:
EPIC: Deep frankensqlite Integration

Current state: storage.rs uses frankensqlite at a basic level — Connection::open, execute, query with parameters, manual BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. This is barely better than raw rusqlite.

Target state: Leverage frankensqlite's two headline innovations:
1. MVCC Concurrent Writers — multiple transcription runs can persist simultaneously without blocking each other (page-level concurrency, SSI for write skew detection)
2. RaptorQ-Pervasive Architecture — self-healing WAL frames, quantitatively bounded data loss (not silent corruption)

Additionally: All DB methods should receive &Cx from asupersync, enabling cancel-safe transactions that roll back cleanly on cancellation. Diagnostic PRAGMAs should expose transaction stats for observability.

The three-table schema (runs, segments, events) is sound but can be enhanced:
- Schema versioning with migration support
- Index optimization for common query patterns (list by time, filter by backend, search transcript text)
- Aggregate views for statistics (runs per backend, average confidence, etc.)

frankensqlite is a LIBRARY, not a runtime — it expects callers to provide &Cx contexts from asupersync. This creates a natural integration point between the two deep dependencies.

Key files: src/storage.rs (current ~428 lines), src/sync.rs (~900 lines)

## Acceptance Criteria
- All DB operations receive &Cx for cancel-safe transactions
- MVCC concurrent writer support verified under contention
- RaptorQ durability layer integrated for crash recovery
- Schema migrations are versioned and idempotent
- Diagnostic queries available for health checks
- All storage tests pass with concurrent access patterns.

When Cx is cancelled during a transaction:
- frankensqlite automatically issues ROLLBACK
- No partial data is written
- The caller receives a cancellation error (not a DB corruption error)

This is a prerequisite for MVCC concurrent writes — MVCC requires Cx for snapshot isolation.

title: Leverage MVCC for concurrent run persistence
description:
frankensqlite's headline innovation: MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) with page-level concurrent writers.

Current state: One run persists at a time (serial execution). With MVCC, multiple runs can write simultaneously without blocking each other.

Use case: When running two-lane execution (parallel backends), both results can be persisted concurrently. Or when the TUI is reading runs while a new transcription is being persisted.

Implementation:
1. Use frankensqlite's MVCC-aware connection mode
2. Each pipeline run gets its own transaction with snapshot isolation
3. Concurrent reads (TUI, robot list) never block concurrent writes
4. Write skew detection via SSI (Serializable Snapshot Isolation) prevents conflicts
5. Page-level First-Committer-Wins for same-page conflicts (rare for our schema since runs have unique IDs)

Testing:
- Spawn 5 concurrent pipeline runs
- All should persist successfully without blocking
- Verify no data corruption or missing records
- Check that reads during writes return consistent snapshots

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two concurrent writers can persist runs simultaneously without corruption
- MVCC isolation: concurrent reads see consistent snapshot
- Contention test: 10 concurrent writers complete without deadlock
- Unit test: parallel persist_report calls produce correct results
- Performance: concurrent writes within 2x single-writer latency.
acceptance_criteria: - Two concurrent writers can persist runs simultaneously without corruption. - MVCC isolation: concurrent reads see consistent snapshot. - Contention test: 10 concurrent writers complete without deadlock. - Unit test: parallel persist_report calls produce correct results. - Performance: concurrent writes within 2x single-writer latency.

title: P1 perf: built-in audio normalization vs ffmpeg batch dominance
description:
Target the realistic batch-ingest workload where franken_whisper can dominate original/scripted Whisper stacks by avoiding subprocess-heavy ffmpeg normalization for common formats.

Candidate levers:
- Reuse decode/resample/write buffers across files.
- Arena or bump allocation for per-run audio scratch.
- SIMD/auto-vectorized stereo mix, f32->i16 quantization, and linear resample loops.
- Branchless fast path for already-normalized 16k mono WAV.
- Cache-oblivious chunking for long audio to reduce peak RSS.

Required measurement:
- `normalize_bench` via rch, crate-scoped, dedicated CARGO_TARGET_DIR.
- Real files: MP3, FLAC, WAV passthrough, MP4/video fallback, 10min and 2h durations when fixtures exist.
- Head-to-head against the original stack normalization path (`ffmpeg`/`whisper.cpp` preprocessing) with original time, franken time, ratio, and RSS.
- Record every win/loss/noise result in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

Acceptance:
- At least one realistic common-audio workload has a measured >20% p95 or wall-time win vs the original preprocessing route, with no transcript/conformance drift.
- No gain or regressions are rejected, documented, and not shipped.
- Quality gates: fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test.

Fallback:
- If high-quality resampling is required or builtin decode fails, retain deterministic ffmpeg fallback and record fallback trigger/evidence.
notes: FINDING (BlackThrush): the core lever is ALREADY implemented. normalize_to_wav_with_timeout (src/audio.rs:128) uses the native symphonia decoder as the PRIMARY path (handles mp3/aac/flac/wav/ogg/alac/wavpack in-process, zero external deps); ffmpeg is fallback-only (exotic/video formats) or when FORCE_FFMPEG_NORMALIZE env is set. So franken_whisper already avoids OpenAI Whisper/whisper.cpp's per-file ffmpeg subprocess spawn + temp-wav I/O -> the 'native dominance over ffmpeg for batch' goal is met by the default. Remaining angle is only: (a) a head-to-head ratio measurement for the ledger (marginal at e2e — normalization is one-time, ~1-5%), and (b) resampler QUALITY (linear -> sinc; that's accuracy, not speed). No speed lever to ship here. Per-crate perf for franken_whisper is encoder-GEMM-bound (bd-4hc0) + decoder-logits-bandwidth-bound; normalization is not on the critical path.

title: Testing Infrastructure: Comprehensive Quality Gates
description:
EPIC: Testing Infrastructure

Testing is a first-class concern. The AGENTS.md mandates:
- cargo fmt --check
- cargo check --all-targets
- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
- cargo test

Each module needs:
- Unit tests: happy path, edge cases, error handling
- Integration tests: file-based transcription, robot mode JSON contracts, SQLite+JSONL sync/recovery, ffmpeg behavior
- E2E tests: full pipeline from audio file to persisted result

Special testing requirements:
1. Cancellation testing: Use asupersync lab runtime to inject cancellation at every pipeline stage, verify no resource leaks
2. Robot mode contract tests: Validate NDJSON output against JSON Schema
3. Backend mock tests: Test pipeline without real backend binaries (mock subprocess output)
4. TUI snapshot tests: Render TUI to buffer, compare against golden snapshots
5. Performance benchmarks: Track regression in processing time, memory usage
6. Sync roundtrip tests: Export → import → compare, verify no data loss

title: Apple Silicon: fused Metal turbo encoder is ~13x behind whisper.cpp Metal on the same host (route now observable)
description:
Measured 2026-08-11 on the M4 Pro dev host (loaded; informational — see PERF_LEDGER 2026-08-11 row):

- large-v3-turbo, jfk.wav (11 s, 1 window): native encoder_window 15.4 s with the FUSED METAL ROUTE CONFIRMED ENGAGED (raw_output.encoder_route == gpu_fused, new introspection), 18.9 s with FRANKEN_WHISPER_GPU=0.
- homebrew whisper-cli 1.8.6 (Metal, -bs 1 -bo 1): 1.20 s TOTAL for the whole job on the same clip/model/host/load.
- Direction is unambiguous: the 2.99x x86 campaign win does not transfer to Apple Silicon; darwin release users are an order of magnitude behind the incumbent on turbo.

Every failure path in gpu_encode_stack used to return false silently; encoder_route (with decline reasons) now closes the silent-fallback blind spot, and the ledger's stage split localizes the gap to ft-kernel-metal::fused::EncoderGpu::forward.

Candidate mechanisms to investigate (in ~/projects/frankentorch/crates/ft-kernel-metal):
1. One command buffer + sync PER LAYER (32 round-trips/window) vs whisper.cpp's whole-graph encode in few command buffers.
2. Naive/untiled Metal GEMM kernels vs MPS/simdgroup_matrix tiles (whisper.cpp uses hand-tuned simdgroup kernels).
3. CPU<->GPU activation copies per layer if activations are not resident end-to-end (conv stem + pos_emb on CPU, then upload).
4. f32 everywhere vs f16 accumulate paths whisper.cpp uses on Metal.

Acceptance: decidable A/B on a quiet M-series host with a pinned darwin whisper.cpp Metal incumbent contract; native turbo whole-job within (initially) 2x of whisper.cpp Metal, with byte-exact-or-ledgered output per AGENTS.md discipline. Requires frankentorch work; coordinate cross-repo.
notes: 2026-08-12: full lever program executed. GPU conv stem (route gpu_fused_stem, FW_GPU_STEM=0 kill switch), half-precision flash K/V tiles + FBK=64 (mha 12.7->9.9ms, e2e transcript identical both routes), f16-resident weights, chunked buffers, clamped edge loads all landed. encoder_window: 15,413ms (first aarch64 measurement) -> 1848-1867ms across 3 consecutive runs. Buffer pool evaluated-not-built (est. tens of ms, below host noise; retry with profiler on quiet host); model-load audit found no aarch64 waste (contention-bound). docs/INCUMBENT_CONTRACT_DARWIN.json pins homebrew whisper-cli 1.8.6 Metal (sha 56b37e5e). REMAINING for a decidable competitive row: darwin port of the incumbent_ab quiescence harness + a quiet M-series host. GEMM still ~2.1 of ~4-5 achievable TFLOPS (MPS-class tiles = the next kernel lever; two-row-block variant graveyarded).

title: P0 perf: ft-kernel-cpu sgemm matrixmultiply->gemm/faer (MEASURED 3.75x) — the e2e wall
description: MEASURED: franken_whisper's e2e is encoder-GEMM-bound, and the GEMM (ft_kernel_cpu::matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32) uses matrixmultiply 0.3 which is 3.75x SLOWER than gemm/faer for the encoder shape [1500,384]x[384,1536]: matrixmultiply 187 GFLOP/s vs gemm/faer 701 GFLOP/s (standalone, x86-64-v3, rayon). Swapping ft-kernel-cpu's matrixmultiply backend to the gemm crate (faer's backend) ~3.75x the sgemm -> ~2x the encoder -> ~1.2x e2e for franken_whisper (and benefits ALL frankentorch users). ft-kernel-cpu already uses unsafe matrixmultiply internally so gemm's unsafe API is fine there; franken_whisper's #![forbid(unsafe_code)] blocks calling gemm directly (faer's safe API is a heavy dep). This is the single biggest remaining e2e lever. Lives in the frankentorch crate (ft-kernel-cpu), out of franken_whisper-cc's scope — needs frankentorch owner or scope expansion.
notes: REFUTED (MEASURED, BlackThrush 2026-06-29). Standalone correctness-gated probe: the gemm crate (faer backend, Parallelism::Rayon(0)=64 threads, x86-64-v3) is TIED 1.01x on the EXACT named shape [1500,384]x[384,1536] (mm 254 vs gemm 252 GF/s) and 1.37x-3.13x SLOWER on production large-v3-turbo encoder shapes (large mlp proj: mm 634 vs gemm 203 GF/s = 3.1x slower). The bead's '187 GF/s matrixmultiply' measured RAW matrixmultiply, NOT ft_kernel_cpu::matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32's tuned rayon-blocked wrapper (kgs4.48/kgs4.61), which already beats the gemm crate. Swapping would REGRESS the encoder. faer-the-library wraps the same gemm microkernels so cannot exceed this ceiling. Full reproduction in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md (2026-06-29 BlackThrush). No encoder-GEMM lever exists here.
close_reason: Refuted by measurement: gemm/faer is tied-to-3.1x-slower than the production ft_kernel_cpu matmul on the real encoder shapes; would regress, not speed up. See docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md 2026-06-29 BlackThrush.

Candidates to PROFILE per-token: (a) logits gemv [51864,384] vs GGML's f16 matmul (GGML may keep activations f16 / use a blocked f16 layout / different threading); (b) per-token overhead — allocations in forward_step, KV-cache growth handling, scratch buffers; (c) flash attention (whisper.cpp uses flash attn=1); (d) sampling/suppress-tokens cost. title: Make speaker-count constraints fail closed and prevent exact-N forced-label collapse
description:
## Outcome

Repair the catastrophic failure mode in which `num_speakers=N` forces every tracklet into one of N labels, fabricates token coverage for missing clusters, and reports `constraints_satisfied=true` even when nearly the whole call collapses into one dominant speaker at zero confidence.

Exact N is a search constraint, not evidence. UNKNOWN and overlap remain legal. If N distinct speakers do not each have adequate independent acoustic or validated hard-hint support, return `unsatisfied_constraints` or `speaker_count_unresolved`; never mutate assignments solely to make N labels appear.

## Verified root cause

The current implementation derives `require_exact_coverage` from the presence of `num_speakers`; this makes UNKNOWN prohibitively expensive, bypasses low-confidence rejection, and then calls `ensure_cluster_coverage` to steal at least one tracklet for every missing label. `constraints_satisfied` checks resulting distinct-label cardinality rather than acoustic evidence or occupancy. Adjacent labels then merge into huge turns, hiding tracklet-level instability.

This behavior violates the documented contract that uncertain speech stays unlabeled and caused the observed long-call collapse. The existing clean synthetic exact-count test proves only that three perfectly separated 500 ms tracklets can yield three labels; it cannot detect this failure family.

## Required redesign

- Replace boolean `require_exact_coverage` with a typed count mode: `Infer`, `Prior`, `Range`, or explicit `HardConstraint`.
- UNKNOWN must remain available in every mode; hard hints, not count cardinality, are the only reason to prohibit UNKNOWN for a specific interval.
- Delete the semantic role of `ensure_cluster_coverage`: no reassignment may occur only to cover a missing label. The function may become a read-only validator if useful; file deletion is not authorized.
- Define per-speaker evidence gates: minimum voiced duration/effective samples, recurrence or sufficiently strong single interval, calibrated separation, profile reliability, and nontrivial posterior mass.
- Define run-level sanity gates: maximum dominant-share compatible with evidence, minimum occupancy, count-posterior entropy/stability, unknown rate, and named-profile coverage.
- `constraints_satisfied` must validate hard constraints, evidence/occupancy, contradictions, and selected count. Cardinality alone is insufficient.
- A soft-enrollment name that fails profile-quality gates remains a named constraint/evidence record but must not become a fabricated profile or forced output label.
- Turn merging must preserve aggregate support/confidence diagnostics so a huge zero-confidence turn cannot appear healthy.

## Regression tests

1. Long synthetic/public-safe three-speaker call with severe near/far level and channel imbalance, many change candidates, and soft intervals for all speakers: exact-N must not collapse into one dominant label while claiming success.
2. N requested but only N-1 speakers acoustically supported: UNKNOWN remains possible and constraints are unsatisfied.
3. One dominant speaker plus two outliers: outliers do not become phantom speakers merely to reach N.
4. Three real speakers with one minority speaker: adequate minority evidence is retained and not merged away.
5. Hard interval for each speaker: interval attribution is enforced, while out-of-interval speech may remain UNKNOWN.
6. Soft intervals: improve posterior/profile evidence without forcing their labels.
7. Exact-count test with identical features: fail closed, deterministic, no arbitrary assignment.
8. Property: increasing requested N without adding evidence can never convert an unsatisfied result into a satisfied one.
9. Property: any `constraints_satisfied=true` speaker has a retained evidence/occupancy record above the declared gate.
10. CLI/robot/persistence round trips preserve count mode, posterior/range, satisfaction reasons, per-hint disposition, per-speaker occupancy, and fallback status.

Use detailed structured test diagnostics: seed, synthetic condition ID, stage, count mode, selected count/range, posterior hash, per-speaker occupancy/confidence, dominant share, UNKNOWN share, hint disposition codes, and invariant failure. Never log transcript/audio content, private source paths, names, or embeddings.

## Acceptance gates

The original collapse is impossible by construction and covered by public-safe regressions. Focused and broad Cargo/UBS gates pass. Public development and held-out evaluation report DER/JER, count accuracy/MAE/NLL, dominant-share and minority-speaker recall, assignment calibration, and selective risk. No default promotion occurs without the parent acoustic-v2 evidence gate.
notes: 2026-07-31 MossyBay completion: replaced split count fields with SpeakerCountRequest::{Infer, Prior, Range, HardConstraint}; removed exact-N label fabrication; retained UNKNOWN in every count mode except interval-local hard hints; added independent voiced-support, recurrence, reliability, separation, occupancy, posterior-mass, dominant-share, hard-assignment, monotonicity, minority-retention, and long imbalanced-call regressions; added typed count outcomes plus per-speaker and per-hint evidence across CLI, robot, schema v5 storage, and JSONL sync. Final proof on the current source snapshot: cargo fmt --all --check PASS; git diff --check PASS; strict remote Linux cargo check --all-targets PASS; storage module 206/206 PASS; process module 37/37 PASS; focused diarization/count tests PASS; UBS src/storage.rs PASS. Full cargo test --lib: 3625 passed, 25 ignored, 2 failed only in pre-existing native-engine gates (known bd-0ivd 20 ms DTW nondeterminism and beam-vs-greedy comma mismatch); every speaker-count, diarization, storage, and sync test passed. Broad clippy remains blocked by unrelated pre-existing warnings in export/native_engine/audio/orchestrator/examples; the one new diarization lint was fixed and changed surface is clean. Public held-out promotion and calibrated automatic count posterior remain explicitly downstream in bd-odj7.13.12 and bd-odj7.13.4.1; this bead closes only the fail-closed constraint safety contract and makes no acoustic-v2 default-promotion claim.
close_reason: Fail-closed speaker-count constraint safety implemented and regression-proved; calibrated posterior and public held-out promotion remain tracked in bd-odj7.13.4.1 and bd-odj7.13.12

title: Profile diarization and noisy multi-speaker workloads vs original stack
description:
## Background
Real users care about meetings, interviews, noisy rooms, overlap, and speaker labels. The existing native-engine artifacts mostly prove ASR throughput on JFK and a long call; they do not measure full diarization/source-separation/VAD workloads against the original whisper-diarization or whisper.cpp TinyDiarize stack.

## Scope
Create a realistic multi-speaker corpus and profile end-to-end franken pipelines against original-stack comparators. Split results by requested feature: `--tiny-diarize`, full `--diarize`, `--vad`, noisy overlap, and long meeting. Only optimize a top-5 measured hotspot. Candidate one-lever families include VAD skip policy, chunk/range scheduling with seam-quality caps, source-separation budget gating, or calibrated backend routing for diarization.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparators: whisper.cpp TinyDiarize for built-in speaker-turn path; legacy whisper-diarization/pyannote stack for full diarization. Record dependency versions and HF-token-free vs token-required modes separately.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard composition B/F: tail-safe adaptive controller and policy-as-data controllers, only with deterministic fallback.
- Alien artifact contract: explicit state/action/loss/posterior/calibration for any routing or budget controller.
- Profiling skill: decompose tail into service, process I/O, queueing, and synchronization.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: latency wins that silently degrade speaker attribution. Safe mode: no promotion without diarization quality caps, segment invariants, text WER, speaker drift report, and deterministic fallback to current static policy.

## Validation
Artifacts: p50/p95/p99 wall, RSS, user CPU, speaker-drift metrics, WER, segment/timestamp conformance, dependency versions, and ratio rows against the original stack. Regressions and neutral results go to docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md.

## Success Criteria
A measured end-to-end win over at least one original diarization workload without quality regression, or a closed negative-evidence report that identifies the next deeper primitive.
close_reason: Closed negative evidence: current 6D heuristic is below-floor; ECAPA model and multi-speaker corpus are prerequisites for an admissible profile

title: native_engine/encoder.rs: whisper audio encoder forward
description:
Implement src/native_engine/encoder.rs: whisper audio encoder forward pass.

SPEC (exact whisper architecture):
- Input mel [n_mel, 3000] for a 30s window (A2).
- conv1: Conv1d(n_mel -> n_state, k=3, stride=1, pad=1) + GELU; conv2: Conv1d(n_state -> n_state, k=3, stride=2, pad=1) + GELU -> [1500, n_state] (time-major).
- + sinusoidal positional embedding (whisper sinusoid: length 1500, channels n_state, log timescale increment ln(10000)/(channels/2-1)) — compute, do NOT read from file (file has it? whisper ggml stores encoder.positional_embedding — USE THE FILE TENSOR for exactness).
- n_audio_layer blocks: x += attn(ln1(x)) [n_head, no mask]; x += mlp(ln2(x)) where mlp = Linear(n,4n)+GELU+Linear(4n,n).
- final ln_post. Output [1500, n_state] reused across all decoder tokens of that window; also precompute per-layer cross K/V projections for decoder (k = x @ Wk (no bias in whisper k!), v = x @ Wv + bv) — note whisper k-projection HAS NO BIAS (verify tensor list: no decoder...attn.key.bias in ggml; handle bias-absent matmuls).
- Weight name map from ggml: encoder.conv{1,2}.{weight,bias}, encoder.positional_embedding, encoder.blocks.N.{attn.query.weight/bias, attn.key.weight, attn.value.weight/bias, attn.out.weight/bias, attn_ln.weight/bias, mlp.0.weight/bias, mlp.2.weight/bias, mlp_ln.weight/bias}, encoder.ln_post.{weight,bias}. VERIFY exact names by dumping tiny.en tensor directory (A1 test prints sorted names -> commit as fixture tests/fixtures/native/tiny_en_tensor_names.txt).
TESTS: shape pipeline test with random small synthetic model (n_state 64, 2 layers — construct weights in-memory); numeric regression: encode jfk.wav window with tiny.en and assert encoder output mean/std/first-8-values against fixture captured ONCE and committed (tests/fixtures/native/jfk_tiny_encoder_stats.json) — guards against silent numeric drift; gated on model presence.
close_reason: Implemented src/native_engine/encoder.rs: whisper audio encoder forward pass. EncoderWeights::from_ggml loads+pre-transposes all linear weights ([out,in]->[in,out]), keeps conv weights flat [Cout,Cin,K], validates every tensor shape against hparams with tensor-named errors (handles ggml [len,1] conv biases). forward() runs conv1(k3 s1 p1)+gelu, conv2(k3 s2 p1)+gelu, transpose mel-major->time-major, adds file positional_embedding (no sinusoid recompute), per-layer residual bidirectional attention (q w+b, k w NO bias, v w+b, out w+b) + mlp(Linear n->4n + gelu + Linear 4n->n), final ln_post; checkpoint() between layers for cancellation. Cross-K/V documented as decoder-owned boundary (returns encoder Mat only). 8 tests pass (synthetic shape/finiteness/input-dependence/bidirectionality/cancellation/guards, transpose roundtrip, gated real tiny.en). Real tiny.en+jfk.wav: out [1500,384] mean=-0.027008 std=1.105640, deterministic. clippy clean, rustfmt clean, cargo check clean.
