title: tiny.en seg-TS is 0.78x (SLOWER than whisper.cpp): remove the NEED for the failed-window retry, not the retry
description:
THE ONLY LOSING CELL vs whisper.cpp. docs/PERF_FRONTIER.md (2026-07-12, matched-greedy, track01 124.5s, tiny.en, 32-core x86): fw 2.24s vs whisper.cpp-greedy 1.76s = 0.78x. Every other matched-greedy cell is a win (turbo 2.07-2.29x, tiny.en no_ts 1.10-1.47x).

CODE-LEVEL DIAGNOSIS (read 2026-07-25, no measurement -- Lane L has no worker):

1. The cost is a REDUNDANT WINDOW DECODE, not a slow kernel. In TS mode result_len is set ONLY by a timestamp token (decode.rs ~2086: tok > tk.timestamp_begin => result_len = i+1). A window that reaches eot with result_len == 0 and !reached_end hits 'Decoder failed with no timestamps closed' and breaks, emitting nothing while advancing a full chunk (the bd-r0qd ~30s content drop). FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW (default-ON since cf41f54) recovers coverage by re-decoding that same seek once with the prompt cleared. Per the frontier that fires on ~2 of 5 windows.

2. THE RETRY IS ALREADY WELL-BUILT -- do NOT try to optimize it. It reuses the first attempt's encode via retry_enc_cache (decode.rs ~1854/1888: same seek => byte-identical enc, no re-encode). Its trigger is guarded by result_len == 0 && !is_no_speech && !force_empty_prompt && prompt_carried, so it fires at most once per seek and NEVER when there is no prompt to clear (retrying with a cleared prompt on an already-empty prompt would decode identical input => provably no redundant fire). Per-window orchestration (DecoderState/cross_kv/mel/prompt) is separately ledgered SUB-FLOOR (<0.25%). There is no slack left in the retry path itself.

3. THEREFORE the only way to remove the 0.78x is to remove the NEED for the retry: make the first attempt not fail. Root cause per the in-code comment: a carried prior-window prompt x int8 decoder numerics makes the decoder emit eot before closing any timestamp.

CANDIDATE FIXES (all change transcript output => all need WER/conformance validation):
  (a) Force-close the window instead of discarding it: on eot with result_len == 0 and tokens decoded, emit the decoded text clamped to the window end rather than dropping and re-decoding. Closest to whisper.cpp's behaviour of always emitting something for a window. Removes BOTH the drop and the retry (2 decodes -> 1).
  (b) Enable the FW_TEMP_FALLBACK ladder (landed but gated off, 42f77b1) -- whisper.cpp's actual mechanism; note it SUPERSEDES FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW when both are set (decode.rs:623), so this is an either/or, and the ladder is strictly more expensive per failure.
  (c) Attack the named cause directly: decode the prompt-conditioned prefix in higher precision so int8 error cannot trigger the premature eot. Narrowest blast radius on transcript output but needs the numerics confirmed first.

OPEN QUESTION THAT DECIDES THE SIZING (needs instrumentation, not a keep-gate A/B): how many tokens does a FAILED attempt actually decode? If the eot really is early (few tokens) the wasted work is small and the observed +0.48s must come from somewhere else; if the decoder runs most of a window and never closes a timestamp, the wasted work is ~a full window decode and fix (a) recovers nearly all of the 0.78x. The in-code comment says 'emit eot early', but 0.48s on a 1.76s baseline over ~2 windows is too large for a genuinely early eot. RESOLVE THIS BEFORE PICKING A FIX.

STATUS: blocked on a measurement window (Lane L = no worker, per ALLOCATION_ADDENDUM 2026-07-25). Requested on the campaign thread. Do not land a transcript-changing decoder fix without WER + conformance validation.

title: diarization not fused with ASR: segment.speaker mostly null, ~1-word lag at turn boundaries
description:
## Summary

Diarization and ASR run on independent timelines and are never fused. The Sortformer
output itself is good — 2 speakers requested and satisfied, mean assignment confidence
0.89/0.93, `fallback_status: not_needed`. The problem is that nothing joins it to the
transcript, so the speaker-attributed result a caller actually wants has to be rebuilt
outside the tool, and the naive join is wrong at exactly the points that matter.

Three concrete defects:

**(a) `segment.speaker` is mostly null.** In a default run of a 45-minute 2-person call,
126 of 207 segments (61%) came back `"speaker": null`, while
`result.diarization.turns` had 885 turns covering the same audio with high confidence.
The evidence to label those segments was present in the same payload and went unused.

**(b) Attribution lags by roughly one word at speaker changes.** Joining word-level
segments to turns by time overlap puts the last word of each turn on the wrong speaker:

```
[00:45.8] Jeff: Jeff. Hey, how are you        <- "Jeff" belongs to the other speaker's "Hey Jeff."
[00:46.8] Hang: doing? Good. Okay, ...        <- "doing?" belongs to the first speaker
```

This is not a constant offset. Measured on a 45-minute two-person call, counting turns
that begin mid-sentence (lowercase first word) out of ~245 turns:

| Approach | Bad boundaries |
|---|---|
| overlap vote only | 122 |
| best global time shift (−0.1 s, swept over ±1.2 s) | ~108 |
| snap each speaker change to the nearest sentence punctuation within ±4 words | **84** |

A global shift barely helps, which rules out a fixed lag and points at the two stages
treating silence/windowing differently. Punctuation snapping needs no timing model and
no extra data — the transcript's own punctuation is the oracle — and it roughly doubles
the improvement. (Earlier numbers I circulated for this, "126 → 108 → 81", came from a
harness that also applied a −0.1 s shift; the figures above are the reproducible ones
with no shift applied.)

**(c) A `speaker_ref` can appear in `turns` but not in `speaker_count.speaker_evidence`**
(an UNKNOWN lane, or an evidence block the acoustic fallback never populated). Any
consumer building a ref→name map from `speaker_evidence` and then indexing it with a
turn's ref will `KeyError` on real output. Whatever fusion ships should treat
`speaker_evidence` as advisory and `turns` as authoritative for the set of refs.

## Why it matters

"Native diarization by default" reads as a promise that the run comes back
speaker-attributed. Today the caller gets two artifacts and a join problem, and the
obvious join silently misattributes the first and last few words of every turn — which is
where short confirmations ("Yeah", "Right", "No, no") live, so those land on the wrong
speaker disproportionately.

## Suggested fix

1. Fuse turns into `segment.speaker` for every segment that any turn overlaps; fall back
   to the neighbouring label rather than `null` when a segment straddles a boundary, and
   expose the per-segment confidence and margin so consumers can audit.
2. Align the two timelines against a single reference. The diarizer and the ASR must
   agree on what the normalized PCM's t=0 is and on how skipped silence is accounted.
3. Snap emitted turn boundaries to token boundaries, preferring sentence-final
   punctuation within a small window. Cheap, model-free, and measurably better than any
   global-shift candidate on real audio.
4. Emit a first-class `result.speaker_segments` (merged consecutive same-speaker
   segments, with text) so the common case needs no client-side reconstruction.

## Acceptance

- No `speaker: null` on segments that overlap a diarization turn.
- Turn boundaries land on token boundaries, not mid-word.
- On a 2-person call, turn-initial words are attributed to the speaker who says them.
- A turn whose `speaker_ref` has no `speaker_evidence` entry does not break attribution.
close_reason: Fixed: projection-fusion-v1. (1) project_diarization_onto_segments now runs a fusion pass after the conservative pass: any segment overlapping a labeled turn takes the max-overlap labeled turn, and timed segments in turn gaps take the nearest labeled turn within 2s (hard-hint turns never extrapolated; untimed segments stay UNKNOWN). (2) Word-level speaker changes snap to the nearest sentence-final punctuation boundary within +/-4 words -- the measured winner over every global time shift. (3) New first-class merged view result.diarization.speaker_segments (consecutive same-speaker runs, byte-faithful joined text, segment_count, duration-weighted turn confidence), built in apply_native_diarization_projection so all six engine lanes get it. Contract doc S6 updated. Timelines confirmed already unified (same normalized WAV t=0). Not done: per-word sub-80ms Sortformer boundary refinement (frozen NeMo parity) and per-segment confidence fields on TranscriptionSegment (79-site schema churn; merged view carries confidence instead).

title: Alien-Artifact Engineering: Adaptive Controllers with Formal Guarantees
description:
EPIC: Alien-Artifact Engineering

The AGENTS.md mandates that any adaptive/runtime decision must include:
- Explicit state space
- Explicit actions
- Loss matrix
- Posterior/confidence terms
- Calibration metric
- Deterministic fallback trigger
- Evidence ledger artifact

No adaptive controller should ship without conservative fallback.

Application areas in franken_whisper:
1. Adaptive Backend Router: Choose backend based on input characteristics (duration, estimated noise, speaker count, available hardware). State space = {input features}. Actions = {backend choice}. Loss matrix = {quality × latency tradeoffs}. Fallback = whisper_cpp (most reliable).

2. Confidence Calibration: Raw confidence scores from different backends are on different scales. Need a calibrated posterior that means "P(word is correct) = confidence_score". Calibration metric = Brier score or ECE (Expected Calibration Error).

3. VAD Threshold Tuning: Voice activity detection threshold affects precision/recall tradeoff. Too aggressive = miss speech. Too conservative = process silence. Adaptive threshold based on audio characteristics.

4. Two-Lane Execution: Run two backends in parallel, compare results, pick the one with higher calibrated confidence. This is the "alien" approach — use redundancy to improve quality.

5. Streaming Quality Controller: When streaming, decide when to emit a "stable" partial transcript vs waiting for more context. State = {accumulated audio, current hypothesis, confidence}. Action = {emit, wait}. Loss = {latency vs accuracy}.

Each controller must produce an evidence ledger artifact documenting the decision process for auditability and debugging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adaptive routing uses explicit state/action/loss/posterior/calibration framework
- Shadow mode emits routing evidence without affecting execution
- Two-lane parallel execution with quality selection works end-to-end
- Evidence ledger persists all routing decisions
- All alien-artifact contract tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive routing uses explicit state/action/loss/posterior/calibration framework. Shadow mode emits routing evidence without affecting execution. Two-lane parallel execution with quality selection works end-to-end. Evidence ledger persists all routing decisions. All alien-artifact contract tests pass.

title: Implement confidence calibration with posterior and Brier score
description:
ALIEN-ARTIFACT: Confidence Calibration

Raw confidence scores from different backends are on different scales. A confidence of 0.8 from whisper_cpp does NOT mean the same as 0.8 from insanely_fast.

STATE SPACE: Raw confidence score (f64), backend that produced it (BackendKind), segment duration (seconds), audio quality estimate (SNR).

ACTIONS: Apply calibration function: calibrated = sigmoid(a * raw + b) per backend. Parameters a, b learned from historical data.

LOSS MATRIX: Overconfident (claim 0.9, actually wrong): high loss. Underconfident (claim 0.3, actually correct): medium loss. Well-calibrated: zero loss.

POSTERIOR: P(word_correct | confidence, backend) as logistic regression.

CALIBRATION METRIC: Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Bin predictions by confidence, compare mean confidence vs actual accuracy per bin. Target ECE < 0.05.

DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK: If < 100 historical data points: pass through raw confidence unchanged. If ECE > 0.15: disable calibration, fall back to raw scores.

Implementation: frankentorch tensor_sigmoid for calibration curve, tensor_backward for parameter fitting (offline). Store calibration parameters in frankensqlite _meta table. Update every 100 runs or on explicit recalibrate command.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Calibration metric tracks: predicted confidence vs actual quality over time
- Metric improves as more runs provide ground truth
- Calibration error (ECE) calculated and logged
- Unit test: perfect predictions produce zero calibration error
- Unit test: random predictions produce high calibration error
- Metric persisted in evidence ledger for trend analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration metric tracks: predicted confidence vs actual quality over time. Metric improves as more runs provide ground truth. Calibration error (ECE) calculated and logged. Unit test: perfect predictions produce zero calibration error. Unit test: random predictions produce high calibration error. Metric persisted in evidence ledger for trend analysis.

title: Implement two-lane execution: parallel backends with quality selection
description:
ALIEN-ARTIFACT: Two-Lane Execution

Run two backends in parallel, compare results, select the best. Use redundancy for quality.

STATE SPACE: Available backends (at least 2 required), audio input characteristics, time budget.

ACTIONS: Run backend A and B in parallel. Compare: confidence, segment count, transcript coherence. Select winner OR merge best segments from both.

LOSS MATRIX: Both succeed pick best (optimal, 2x cost). One fails other succeeds (failover benefit). Both fail (no worse than single). Time budget exceeded (cancel slower, use faster).

SELECTION CRITERIA (ranked): Higher calibrated mean confidence, more segments, better speaker separation, shorter processing time (tiebreaker).

DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK: If only one backend available: single-lane. If time budget < 2x expected time: single-lane.

Implementation: Use asupersync parallel regions (one per backend). Both write to temp dirs. Main region waits for both (or cancels slower after timeout). Compare using calibrated confidence scores. MVCC enables concurrent persistence.

This naturally exercises deep asupersync (parallel regions, cancellation, bounded cleanup) and deep frankensqlite (MVCC concurrent writes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two backends execute in parallel on same input
- Quality comparison selects winner based on: confidence scores, segment alignment, timing precision
- Losing backend result discarded (or persisted as shadow)
- Parallel execution respects Cx cancellation
- Unit test: higher-quality result is selected
- Unit test: cancel during parallel execution cleans up both backends
- Performance: parallel overhead under 10% vs single backend.

title: REOPENED: weight-stationary f16 GEMV tile — prior REJECT benched cross_attn_k/v, which stopped using gemv_f16_batch on 2026-07-02
description:
LEDGER-INTEGRITY REOPEN (cc_fw, 2026-07-10). The 2026-07-09 REJECT of a token-block weight-stationary tile for gemv_f16_batch_rows is INVALID: its stated consumer does not exist.

THE FALSE PREMISE. The row claims: "cross_attn_k/v.forward(encoder_out) at tq=1500 loads NO w_i8 (they only get .dequant_to_f32_if(cross_proj_f32_enabled()), DEFAULT OFF) => they route to the f16 batch (gemv_f16_batch -> gemv_f16_batch_rows)."
Reality: cross_proj_f32_enabled() is `const DEFAULT_ON: bool = true` (mod.rs:701), flipped default-ON by a674b49 on 2026-07-02 ("flip cross-proj f32 sgemm DEFAULT-ON - 2.25x now active"), SEVEN DAYS before the row was written. Its doc: "Route the per-window cross-K/V PROJECTIONS through dequant-once f32 tiled sgemm INSTEAD of the f16 batched GEMV." decoder.rs:671,679 hand cross-K/V to WeightMat::F32 => nn::matmul_bias. Cross-K/V therefore contributes 0% of gemv_f16_batch self-time. The reject was benched at the CROSS shape [1500,1280]x[1280,1280], which that kernel no longer sees.

THE REAL CONSUMER. gemv_f16_batch has exactly one production call site (decoder.rs:345; nn.rs:5558 is a unit test), reachable only by WeightMat::F16 linears at tq>1 with no w_i8. Per decoder.rs:312, mlp_2 (fc2) is deliberately excluded from the int8 batch path because it carries a w_i8_block copy -- "those stay on the f16 batch path". So the true consumer is fc2 AT PREFILL: tq = prompt length (single digits), k=5120, n=1280.

WHAT TO DO. Re-measure the weight-stationary token-block tile at the fc2-prefill shape, NOT the cross shape. Expect a small prize: prefill runs once per window, not per token. Same-binary A/B (both arms one binary, one rch invocation; flip via a setter, never an env var). Record the self-time.

ALSO CORRECTED (no revert needed): the LANDED dot_f16c_2col / M2col win (2026-07-09, byte-exact, default-on, 1.212x) attributes itself to "the ~2% e2e cross_kv span" via the same false premise. The kernel result stands (bit-for-bit identical); its E2E ATTRIBUTION does not. Its real beneficiary is fc2 prefill. Do not carry "~2% e2e cross_kv" forward as this lever payoff.

title: franken-decision to_evidence_ledger() panics on the degenerate native-only fallback audit (worked around in backend/mod.rs)
description:
UPSTREAM (franken-decision crate, v0.3.4/0.3.5).

On a native-only install (no external whisper.cpp / insanely-fast / whisper-diarization BRIDGE backend present) the adaptive router computes observed_state == 2 ("no bridge backends"). franken-decision's decision_evaluate then engages the deterministic fallback and returns an internally-inconsistent DecisionAuditEntry. Converting that entry via its own DecisionAuditEntry::to_evidence_ledger() (which calls EvidenceLedgerBuilder::build().expect("audit entry should produce valid evidence ledger")) PANICS:

  Validation([PosteriorNotNormalized { sum: -0.0 },
              CalibrationOutOfRange { value: 0.5 },
              ChosenExpectedLossMismatch { action: "try_whisper_cpp", chosen: -0.0, mapped: -0.0 }])

i.e. franken-decision produces an audit that its own builder rejects, and the conversion PANICS (via .expect) instead of returning an error — killing every transcription on the common native-only path.

Repro: `franken_whisper youtube <url>` (or `transcribe` with backend=auto) on a machine whose only usable backend is the native engine. The in-process decoder falls back to ffmpeg, routing evaluates, and the panic aborts the run.

ROOT CAUSE (in franken-decision): the fallback branch of decision_evaluate emits an audit with an empty/unnormalized posterior_snapshot and a chosen expected_loss that does not match expected_loss_by_action[chosen]; and to_evidence_ledger() uses .expect() rather than returning Result.

RECOMMENDED UPSTREAM FIX: (a) decision_evaluate must not emit an unbuildable audit for the fallback branch — populate/normalize posterior_snapshot and keep chosen expected_loss == expected_loss_by_action[chosen]; and/or (b) DecisionAuditEntry::to_evidence_ledger() should return Result<EvidenceLedger, _> instead of panicking.

WORKAROUND ALREADY LANDED in franken_whisper (src/backend/mod.rs, the routing decision function): the evidence ledger is a diagnostic, so guard its construction — skip the conversion when the audit posterior is empty/unnormalized (the observed degeneracy), with catch_unwind as a safety net, degrading to no evidence entry and recording an 'evidence_ledger_conversion_failed' router event. Mirrors the existing "diagnostics never kill transcription" guards (failed posterior update, contract-validation fallback).

VERIFIED: patched native-only `transcribe` returns real segments with zero panics on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

ARCHITECTURE DECISION (settled with Jeffrey 2026-06-04):
- Build on frankentorch crates (path deps ../frankentorch/crates/*): ft-kernel-cpu provides rayon-parallel sgemm/sgemm_block (matrixmultiply-backed), softmax_dim_tensor_contiguous_f32, gelu; ft-core provides DenseTensor with F16/F32 storage (half crate); ft-serialize provides load_safetensors (f16->f32). - franken_whisper implements the whisper-specific layer: ggml .bin parser, log-mel frontend, BPE tokenizer, encoder/decoder assembly with KV cache, decode loop. Use a THIN internal facade that calls ft-kernel-cpu kernels directly (avoids ft-api tape overhead per decoder token; keeps KV cache management local).
- frankenjax (fj-interpreters/fj-lax) = optional differential-verification oracle for attention/softmax numerics in the conformance harness (feature-gated; it is scalar-loop slow but oracle-verified against real JAX).
- New module dir src/native_engine/ (genuinely new functionality, sanctioned exception to no-new-files rule).

MODEL FORMAT GROUND TRUTH (verified against ~/models/whisper/ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin and ggml-tiny.en.bin 2026-06-04):
- magic 0x67676d6c ("lmgg" LE); 11 x i32 hparams: n_vocab, n_audio_ctx, n_audio_state, n_audio_head, n_audio_layer, n_text_ctx, n_text_state, n_text_head, n_text_layer, n_mels, ftype. (large-v3-turbo: 51866/1500/1280/20/32/448/1280/20/4/128/1)

- tensor directory until EOF: i32 n_dims, i32 name_len, i32 ftype, n_dims x i32 dims, name bytes, then data aligned; ftype 0=f32 1=f16 (quantized variants exist; f32/f16 required, quantized = follow-up bead).

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATION: tiny/base near-real-time on 8-16 cores; large-v3-turbo functional but slow on CPU (~1-2x audio duration). That is FINE: the rollout governance keeps the bridge primary until the native engine earns promotion via conformance + benchmarks. Honesty first, speed second.

title: native_engine/decoder.rs: whisper text decoder forward + KV cache
description:

title: REOPENED: i7 rowblock coarsening + i7 bias specialization gate the TOP owned frame (~28% self-time on turbo); their ratios are substrate-invalid
description:
REOPENED 2026-07-10 (cc_fw) after an in-situ profile CORRECTED my own audit.

MY AUDIT WAS WRONG. I claimed these rows have "0% self-time in the default engine", citing enc_int8_enabled() = DEFAULT_ON:false and encoder.rs:483 ("Default off => all i7 fields stay None"). I quoted the comment on the FIRST branch of an if/else-if chain and never read past it. The THIRD branch is `else if super::enc_attn_out_i8i32_for(&model.hparams)` -- the landed DEFAULT quality-safe int8 encoder -- which builds attn_q_i7/attn_k_i7/attn_v_i7/mlp_fc_i7 and routes attn.out through the full-i8 i32-accumulate GEMM. calibrated_encoder_int8_model() matches large-v3-turbo AND tiny.en.

MEASURED IN-SITU (perf -F 299, prebuilt release-perf e2e_probe, large-v3-turbo, jfk x8, load amortized, NO build):
  dot_maddubs_i7_m2n4                     14.63% self
  matmul_bias_i7_quantized::{closure#0}    9.91%
  encoder::matmul_bias_i8::{closure#1}     2.74%   (attn.out i8xi32)
  quantize_act_i7::{closure#0}             0.88%
  => i7 int8 encoder GEMM = ~28.2% self-time. THE HOTTEST OWNED CODE IN THE ENGINE.
For comparison: external matrixmultiply sgemm 14.31%, SDPA 11.46%, rayon overhead 11.25%.

SO THESE ROWS GATE A ~28% FRAME, AND THEIR RATIOS ARE INADMISSIBLE. As the audit correctly found, both A/Bs ran the candidate and the legacy arm as TWO SEPARATE rch bench invocations with FW_I7_ROWBLOCK_MIN_LEN flipped between them ("candidate coarse split (default 8, hz2)" vs "legacy original split (=1, hz2)"). rch has no --worker flag and ratios are not worker-invariant, so a two-invocation A/B is invalid. The legacy arm own spread is +/-1.30 ms on 12.79 ms (cv ~10%). A do-not-retry row over a 28% frame cannot rest on that.

PREREQUISITE FOR ANY RE-MEASURE: FW_I7_ROWBLOCK_MIN_LEN is a OnceLock env read, so it CANNOT flip inside one binary. It needs a runtime setter, exactly like set_sdpa_poly_exp / set_sgemm_tile_balanced. Add the setter first; then bench both arms in ONE binary / ONE rch invocation, arms interleaved inside a single measured routine, black_box on inputs and full output, with a NULL CONTROL (arm vs itself) to calibrate the floor, and record self-time per arm.

franken_whisper now DOES bench remotely: RCH_CONFIG_DIR=<scratch copy with total_timeout_ms 600000 + excludes> RCH_DISABLE_CONFIG_CACHE=1 RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR rch exec -- cargo bench -p franken_whisper --bench <name>  (verified on hz2, disk flat).

LESSON: static reachability is only as good as the branch you stopped reading at. Read the whole else-if chain, and confirm with a profile. A profile caught this in one command.

title: Measure live/speculative streaming TTFT vs original streaming baselines
description:
## Background
`franken_whisper` claims real-time NDJSON and speculative dual-model streaming, but the current perf artifacts focus on batch transcription. For real users and agents, time-to-first-token/partial, correction latency, and p95 event latency matter as much as total wall time.

## Scope
Build a live/streaming benchmark that compares franken robot/speculative output against original streaming-capable baselines where available (`whisper.cpp` partial output or other original Whisper streaming harness). Measure TTFT, partial cadence, p95 event latency, correction/retraction rate, end-to-end wall, and quality drift. Optimize only after profiling a top-5 hotspot.

## Baseline Comparator
Original comparator: `whisper.cpp` streaming/partial mode when available; otherwise explicitly label the baseline as OpenAI/whisper.cpp batch fallback and do not claim streaming superiority. Franken paths: robot NDJSON, speculative fast+quality, and TTY transcript-control path if exercised.

## Alien / Optimization Mapping
- Graveyard composition B: tail-safe adaptive controller for speculation windows.
- Graveyard sections 12.1, 12.13, 12.16: conformal/calibration/change-point guards for correction thresholds.
- Alien artifact contract: state space, actions, loss, posterior/confidence, calibration, deterministic fallback, evidence ledger.

## Risks / Safe Mode
Risk: better TTFT with unacceptable correction churn or WER. Safe mode: fixed deterministic window and current correction tolerance. Fallback trigger: Brier/coverage breach, correction-rate SLO breach, WER regression, or p95 latency regression.

## Validation
Artifacts: TTFT/TPOT-like metrics, p50/p95/p99 event latency, correction stats, WER drift, calibration ledger snapshot, original-vs-franken ratio row, conformance/golden output, and negative-evidence row for abandoned adaptive policies.

## Success Criteria
A measured live/streaming win with bounded correction quality, or an explicit closeout showing which original comparator or workload blocks the claim.

title: native long-form window drop loses ~30s of speech with no signal in --json output
description:
## Summary

When a long-form decode window closes without a timestamp, the native engine drops
~30 s of audio. It logs this to **stderr only**. `result.warnings` in the `--json`
payload does not mention it, so an agent consuming the documented machine surface has
no way to learn that a chunk of the recording is missing from the transcript.

Worse, the naive recovery — re-transcribe that region as its own input — **reproduces the
drop**, so a caller who notices the hole can still fail to fill it.

## Evidence (v0.7.2, 45-minute two-person call, `--backend whisper-cpp`)

stderr:

```
long-form window closed no timestamp — ~30 s of audio dropped
(set FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW=1 to attempt prompt-reset recovery; see bd-r0qd)
seek_sec=514.0 no_speech_prob=5.6e-10 avg_logprob=-0.111
```

`--json` from that same run:

```json
"warnings": ["using deterministic CPU normalization",
             "native frame-RMS energy evidence available"]
```

The window is 514.0–544.0 s. `result.segments` jumps straight across it.

**The dropped audio is dense two-speaker speech, not silence.** Independent evidence:

- The run's own diarization reports **32 s of voiced turn coverage** inside that 30 s
  span (>30 because both speakers overlap), across 15 turns alternating between
  `SPEAKER_00` and `SPEAKER_01` with confidences 0.7–0.99.
- ffmpeg `volumedetect` over 2-second buckets reads −19 dB to −31 dB throughout — normal
  conversational level for this recording.
- `no_speech_prob` was **5.6e-10**: the engine itself was certain this was speech when it
  discarded it.
- Transcribing 512–530 s and 528–546 s as two short slices returns ~60 words of ordinary
  conversation (a speaker rebutting a concern, then discussing a version that had
  finished building) that appear nowhere in the full-file transcript.

**Recovery is not as simple as re-slicing.** Re-transcribing 508–552 s as one 44-second
input (with `FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW=1` set) returned only the material from *either side*
of the hole — it dropped the same 514–544 region again. Only slicing into sub-30-second
chunks, so the region does not sit at a long-form window boundary, recovered the content.
That suggests the trigger is tied to window placement over this particular audio
(the region is heavy crosstalk), and that it is deterministic rather than flaky.

## Why it matters

Silent content loss is the failure mode a transcription tool must never have. Everything
downstream — diarization, cleanup, summaries — inherits the hole with no signal that it
exists. The recovery mechanism (`FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW=1`) exists but is off by default,
is discoverable only by reading stderr (which agents routinely discard), and in this case
did not actually recover the window.

## Suggested fix

1. Emit a structured warning into `result.warnings` **and** an addressable
   `result.dropped_windows: [{start_sec, end_sec, reason, no_speech_prob, avg_logprob}]`
   whenever a window is discarded. This is the minimum fix: make the loss visible to the
   machine surface.
2. Make `FW_RETRY_FAILED_WINDOW=1` the **default**, with the env var repurposed to opt
   *out*. A retry that occasionally costs a few seconds beats losing 30 s of speech.
3. Make the retry actually work for this case: retry with a **shifted window boundary**
   (and/or a shorter window), since re-running the same geometry reproduces the failure.
   A sub-30 s re-slice of the same audio decodes fine.
4. If retry still fails, keep the window in the output as an explicit
   `[audio dropped 514.0–544.0]` marker rather than closing the gap silently, so the
   omission survives into artifacts instead of looking like continuous speech.

## Acceptance

- A run that drops a window reports it in `result.warnings` and in a structured field.
- Retry-on-failed-window is on by default and varies window geometry before giving up.
- A recording containing this failure either transcribes the window or marks it.
- `fw robot`/NDJSON surfaces carry the same signal.
close_reason: Fixed: dropped long-form windows are structural, not stderr-only. DecodeOutput.dropped_windows records {start_sec,end_sec,reason,no_speech_prob,avg_logprob,retried}; exported additively in raw_output (native-v2) with decode_work retry counters; orchestrator surfaces each drop into RunReport.warnings (with recovery guidance), evidence ledger (native_decode_dropped_windows), and a backend.dropped_windows stage event, so --json and robot NDJSON both carry the signal. Retry-on-failed-window was already default-on (ledgered 2026-07-24); the stale opt-in message was corrected and DISCREPANCIES.md updated. Residual: escalating a failed retry into the temperature-fallback ladder remains open under bd-r0qd/bd-c9uv (behavior change needing its own ledger row).

title: EPIC: Rust-native acoustic speaker diarization with supervised intervals
description:
GOAL
Build a waveform-aware, memory-safe, deterministic Rust-native speaker diarization subsystem that replaces the current six-dimensional temporal/lexical heuristic. The subsystem must distinguish speakers using actual acoustic evidence: spectral envelope and vocal-tract cues, fundamental-frequency and harmonic structure, loudness/distance, spectral tilt and muffling, channel distortion, and multiscale acoustic regime changes. It must accept agent-provided known timestamp intervals as hard or soft supervision for building within-run speaker profiles.

ARCHITECTURE
The canonical flow is normalized 16 kHz PCM -> VAD speech mask -> 25 ms/10 ms acoustic frames -> voice/channel feature views -> multiscale regime-change detection -> speaker-homogeneous microturns -> robust profile sufficient statistics -> deterministic constrained clustering -> temporal smoothing/unknown rejection -> diarized turn timeline -> DTW word-boundary transcript projection. Acoustic diarization is a central post-ASR pipeline stage, not logic hidden inside a backend adapter.

FIRST-PRINCIPLES CONSTRAINTS
- Keep speaker/voice features separate from channel/location features so a stable speakerphone signature helps within a call without becoming permanent identity.
- Pitch is evidence, never a gender label and never sufficient alone.
- Full raw-audio CWT and dense all-pairs clustering over multi-hour calls are forbidden as defaults; use bounded streaming aggregation, inexpensive Haar-like multiscale differences, tracklets, and capped prototypes.
- Unknown/insufficient-evidence and overlap-suspected are first-class honest outcomes.
- Known intervals have typed schema, content hash, confidence, provenance, hard/soft semantics, boundary guards, voiced-frame filtering, and conflict validation.
- Raw voice profiles are potentially biometric: ephemeral by default; durable profile vectors require explicit opt-in.
- Preserve cancellation, stage budgets, deterministic replay, robot schemas, SQLite-as-source-of-truth, JSONL recovery, and evidence-led rollout.

DEPENDENCY POLICY
Production should reuse or factor the existing fixed 400-sample native Whisper spectrum path without changing transcription bytes. FrankenSciPy FFT/signal/cluster components begin as differential-test oracles; broad fsci-signal/fsci-cluster production dependencies require matched performance and dependency evidence. FrankenNumPy is not required for v1. ECAPA-TDNN remains an optional later engine implementing the same profile/turn contract.

DEFINITION OF DONE
All child beads close with the mandatory fmt/check/clippy/test gates green; permutation-invariant DER/JER and change-point scoring exist; agent hints are validated and demonstrably influence profiles; central pipeline/CLI/robot/storage/JSONL integration works; deterministic replay and cancellation are proven; performance and negative evidence are ledgered; the old heuristic is no longer presented or selected as native acoustic diarization.

## Success Criteria

All child beads close with their named unit, end-to-end, recovery, cancellation, replay, corpus, performance, privacy, and rollout gates satisfied. The central native path uses real acoustic evidence, known intervals work, uncertainty is honest, and the lexical heuristic is neither selected nor mislabeled.

title: Specify acoustic diarization v1 contract, loss model, scorers, and replay evidence
description:
BACKGROUND
The current native contract checks segment monotonicity and allows inexact speaker labels, which is insufficient for a waveform diarizer because speaker IDs are permutation-invariant and turns may not align with ASR segments.

SCOPE
Define acoustic-diarization-v1 before implementation. Specify the state space, actions, loss matrix, posterior/confidence terms, calibration metrics, deterministic fallback triggers, feature-schema versioning, replay evidence fields, and privacy boundary. Define independent diarized turns, unknown and overlap-suspected outcomes, speaker-count constraints, hard/soft hint semantics, label canonicalization, cancellation checkpoints, and bounded-resource guarantees.

SCORING
Implement or specify permutation-invariant DER and JER, change-point precision/recall/F1 with explicit collar, hint adherence, speaker-confusion time, false split/merge diagnostics, unknown rate, Brier score, expected calibration error, replay determinism, and peak-memory/RTF reporting. Synthetic audio is unit evidence only, never corpus accuracy proof.

DELIVERABLE
A self-contained contract and scorer API that every implementation and later ECAPA engine must satisfy.

## Acceptance Criteria

A versioned acoustic-diarization-v1 contract exists; permutation-invariant scoring and change-point scoring have happy-path, permutation, boundary, empty, unknown, overlap, and malformed-input tests; the adaptive decision contract names state, actions, loss, confidence, calibration, fallback, and evidence; no accuracy threshold is claimed without retained corpus evidence.

## Conservative Fallback

If evidence is insufficient or calibration is outside its valid envelope, leave inferred speaker unset or UNKNOWN. If hard hints exist, preserve only their attributable intervals and keep the remainder unknown. Never create a second speaker merely to satisfy min_speakers when acoustic evidence cannot support one; instead return an explicit unsatisfied-constraint report unless policy requests a hard error.

## Metric Semantics

DER must be computed after optimal speaker permutation and separately report missed speech, false alarm, and speaker confusion. JER is speaker-averaged. Change-point evaluation names its collar and whether overlap is scored. Speaker confidence calibration is evaluated only on label-matched ground truth and must include coverage so a system cannot appear calibrated by returning unknown everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned acoustic-diarization-v1 contract exists; permutation-invariant scoring and change-point scoring have happy-path, permutation, boundary, empty, unknown, overlap, and malformed-input tests; the adaptive decision contract names state, actions, loss, confidence, calibration, fallback, and evidence; no accuracy threshold is claimed without retained corpus evidence.

title: Freeze a versioned diarization scorer, manifest schema, and leakage audit
description:
## Outcome

Create the authoritative metric/scorer contract before further tuning.

## Work

- Specify DER/JER, collar/overlap policy, change metrics, attribution/count, overlap, hints, unknown/selective risk, Brier/ECE, RTF/RSS, and determinism hashes.
- Version reference, hypothesis, corpus manifest, split, normalization, configuration, and result schemas.
- Validate interval geometry, label equivalence mapping, ignored regions, and overlap semantics with stable errors.
- Add split-leakage checks covering recordings, speakers where known, derived clips, augmentations, and enrollment intervals.
- Produce privacy-safe summaries and opaque hashes; reject paths/content from confidential sources in retained output.

## Tests and success

title: Extend the frozen scorer for count posteriors, occupancy collapse, and word attribution
description:
## Outcome

Version the frozen scorer and manifest/result schemas to evaluate automatic count distributions, phantom/collapsed speaker behavior, and context-assisted word attribution without weakening the existing DER/JER authority.

## Additions

- Count: exact accuracy, MAE, confusion matrix, posterior NLL/Brier, top-k/credible-set coverage, entropy, unresolved rate, calibration by K/domain/duration.
- Per speaker/run: voiced and quality-adjusted effective occupancy, recurrence, minority-speaker recall, dominant-speaker share, UNKNOWN share, phantom-speaker rate, collapsed-reference-speaker rate, supported-profile/name coverage.
- Constraints/hints: hard satisfaction by reason, soft evidence gain, per-hint accepted/downweighted/quarantined/rejected counts, contradiction rate.
- Context/transcription: WDER, cpWER or declared equivalent, anonymous-cluster attribution versus name/role mapping, boundary error at word edges, contextual revision gain/harm, query efficiency.
- Temporal/overlap: iteration gain/rollback, overlap-aware metrics, fixed-lag/offline disagreement.

Keep every metric label-permutation invariant where appropriate and explicitly declare collar, overlap, UNKNOWN, unresolved count, and rejected-coverage policies. Do not average away recording-level collapse: report macro and micro summaries plus quantiles/worst-case gates.

## Corpora and protocol

Reuse the immutable AMI/AISHELL-4/VoxConverse/CALLHOME registry and add only provenance-cleared descriptors if a required condition is absent. Stratify by speaker count, duration, overlap, near/far/channel mismatch, imbalance, short turns, and same-gender/similar-pitch where metadata permits. Follow the SDBench principle of consistent multi-domain evaluation but do not copy its runtime or datasets blindly.

Freeze development and held-out parameter-selection rules before evaluation. Private local recordings may produce only aggregate opaque corroboration and never promotion authority by themselves.

## Tests

Hand-computed golden examples for every metric; permutation invariance; one/many/zero/unresolved speakers; exact posterior bins; missing bins; invalid normalization; dominant collapse; minority omission; phantom outlier; UNKNOWN; overlap; name-map errors; ASR insertions/deletions; macro/micro divergence; deterministic serialization; schema/recovery errors; leakage audit.

Detailed test output names metric, fixture ID, mapping, expected/actual numerator and denominator, count mode, and policy version without transcript/audio/private paths or identities.

## Success criteria

The scorer catches the previously observed 99% dominant-speaker collapse even if distinct-label cardinality equals the requested count. Existing scorer-v1 goldens remain semantically reproduced or discrepancies are explicitly versioned. Public development/held-out reports are reproducible from opaque manifests, and bd-odj7.13.12 plus bd-odj7.10.7 consume the new authority before any promotion.

title: Roll out acoustic diarization, retire lexical heuristic claims, and adapt ECAPA as optional engine
description:
## Outcome

Roll out the corrected and accuracy-certified acoustic diarization path through explicit Shadow -> Validated -> Fallback -> Primary -> Sole stages, retire lexical-heuristic accuracy claims, and keep ECAPA and other advanced modes independently gated.

## Current state

Fail-closed rollout resolution, provenance events, explicit engine/fallback semantics, lexical-evidence quarantine, common optional-neural contract, privacy guards, and schema-v4 persistence/recovery have been implemented. The default remains Shadow. This issue stays open because implementation and broad code proof are not accuracy or performance authority.

## Required authorities

Report and retain separately:

1. DTW/native product-path correctness proof.
2. Focused acoustic unit/property/e2e/robot/persistence proof.
3. Frozen public core-v2 corpus/scorer/ablation proof.
4. Confidence/unknown calibration proof.
5. Same-snapshot, same-host performance and bounded-memory certification.
6. Broad mandatory Cargo/UBS hygiene gates.
7. Optional-mode public evidence for overlap/query/streaming/multichannel/fusion.
8. Separate ECAPA real-weight conformance, corpus, license, and performance proof.

A synthetic fixture, one private recording, a private aggregate bootstrap, external published results, code review, or a broad Cargo pass cannot substitute for the missing authority.

## Rollout state and actions

- State: engine/mode, evidence artifact hashes, schema/calibration/config versions, public held-out gates, determinism, privacy, error rate, RTF/RSS, fallback eligibility, and rollback alarms.
- Actions: remain Shadow, advance one stage, hold, demote one or more stages, disable an optional mode, or reject an unsupported request.
- Loss: accuracy/calibration regression, hard-hint violation, privacy/schema/contract failure, nondeterministic replay, latency/memory regression, unavailable fallback, and misleading public claims.
- Confidence: promotion confidence is derived only from predeclared held-out/equivalence gates and retained artifacts, never from the runtime speaker confidence.
- Fallback: any hard contract/privacy/determinism violation immediately demotes to the last proven stage; statistically supported quality/performance regression triggers the declared rollback threshold.

## Work

- Bind every behavior/default lever (including FW_/FRANKEN_WHISPER_ OnceLock flags) to a stage and ledger entry; audit DEFAULT_ON and get_or_init before each release claim.
- Update README, architecture, feature parity, native contract, discrepancies, recovery runbook, robot schema, performance ledger, and negative-evidence ledger to match live source and current proof.
- Ensure public labels distinguish classical acoustic v1/v2, optional ECAPA/neural, external, lexical-quarantined, unknown, fallback, and unavailable.
- Make core-v2 promotion independent of unfinished optional modes; each optional mode has its own stage and rollback trigger.
- Remove or quarantine the old six-dimensional lexical/text-temporal clusterer so it cannot be selected or described as acoustic/neural evidence.
- Provide stable rollout decision events in robot JSON/NDJSON and durable storage, with exact snapshot/evidence fingerprints.
- Exercise upgrade/downgrade, restart, cancellation, missing calibration/model, and rollback alarms.

## Promotion gates

- Shadow -> Validated: M0 product correctness, focused tests, public development improvement, schema/privacy correctness.
- Validated -> Fallback: frozen public held-out core gates pass and the safe mode is reliable enough to serve as an explicit fallback.
- Fallback -> Primary: same-snapshot performance/memory, calibration, durability, deterministic replay, and rollback drills pass.
- Primary -> Sole: older mode removal is justified by a documented operating envelope and no required unsupported fallback remains.
- ECAPA/advanced modes advance independently and do not change core defaults through association.

## Success criteria

Docs, code, robot schema, SQLite/JSONL, environment flags, and evidence ledger agree exactly; no lexical heuristic is selected or mislabeled; core and optional proof states are separated; all rollback triggers are tested; and any default change names the retained artifact hashes and last proven fallback.

title: EPIC: Acoustic diarization accuracy v2 and production certification
description:
## Outcome

Turn the current dependency-light acoustic diarizer into a correctness-first, measurable, substantially more accurate speaker attribution system while preserving the project's Rust-native, memory-safe, bounded-memory, agent-friendly design.

## Why this epic exists

The current implementation is a valuable v1 baseline, but present evidence exposes three separate blockers that must not be conflated:

- The native CLI acoustic path rejects at least one valid DTW projection shape, so the actual product path is not yet trustworthy even when lower-level diarization succeeds.
- On the current private local bootstrap set, change-point F1 was 0 at a 250 ms collar and nearest-boundary error remained large. These are aggregate diagnostics only; no confidential audio, transcript text, filenames, identities, or derived content may enter this repository.
- Hard contextual hints are now obeyed, but held-out conditional speaker accuracy regressed relative to the unhinted baseline, indicating profile contamination, representation mismatch, or overconfident metric adaptation rather than a simple hint-adherence failure.

The existing compact representation (six cepstral coefficients, one pitch coordinate, harmonicity, plus a lightly weighted channel vector) and fixed global thresholds cannot express or calibrate the full range of within-call voice, distance, device, codec, and muffling regimes described by the product mission.

## Scope

This epic coordinates:

1. End-to-end DTW projection correctness.
2. A trustworthy, versioned evaluation and failure-attribution loop.
3. Acoustic representation v2 with richer voice/channel views and per-recording robust normalization.
4. Calibrated multiscale speaker-change inference.
5. Enrollment hygiene, multi-modal speaker profiles, and supervised within-call metric adaptation.
6. Probabilistic constrained clustering, speaker-count stability, temporal smoothing, calibrated confidence, and conservative unknown fallback.
7. Overlap handling and calibrated fusion of native acoustic, DTW, silence, and optional TinyDiarize evidence.
8. Agent feedback, streaming correction semantics, optional multichannel cues, performance certification, and an optional native ECAPA-TDNN tier behind the same embedding contract.
9. Unit, property, metamorphic, integration, robot-schema, persistence, recovery, determinism, cancellation, privacy, and long-call tests.

## Architecture principles

- Preserve explicit separation between voice identity features and channel/environment features; channel evidence may refine a speaker profile but must not silently become speaker identity.
- Treat contextual intervals as constraints with provenance and confidence, not labels that bypass acoustic validation.
- Every adaptive decision must define state, actions, loss, posterior/confidence, calibration metric, fallback trigger, and evidence artifact.
- Keep deterministic, dependency-light acoustic inference as the safe fallback. Optional learned embeddings must implement the existing common contract and may never become required for basic diarization.
- All scoring and promotion claims must be tied to a versioned scorer, corpus manifest or local private-evaluation fingerprint, configuration fingerprint, and retained machine-readable evidence.
- Private recordings and transcripts remain outside the project tree at all times. Repository artifacts may contain only aggregate, non-identifying metrics and opaque fingerprints.
- Do not weaken validation merely to accept malformed time geometry. Normalize each explicit input representation into a typed canonical timeline and reject true contradictions with stable robot error codes.

## Explicit non-goals

- No Python runtime dependency in the native path.
- No vendored third-party diarization service.
- No claim of production accuracy from synthetic-only tests or from one private recording.
- No lexical speaker guessing as a substitute for acoustic evidence.
- No default-on promotion without the named accuracy, calibration, determinism, memory, and latency gates.

## Milestones and promotion gates

### M0 — Correct product path

The native CLI/robot path accepts valid DTW word timing, rejects invalid timing deterministically, and round-trips speaker turns through JSON/NDJSON and SQLite/JSONL without loss.

### M1 — Measurement authority

A versioned scorer and licensed public evaluation protocol produce DER/JER, speech miss/false alarm, confusion, boundary precision/recall/F1, attribution accuracy, overlap-aware scores, hint adherence, Brier/ECE calibration, unknown precision/recall, RTF, peak RSS, and determinism hashes with stage-specific failure attribution.

### M2 — Classical acoustic v2

On declared public development and held-out sets, the dependency-light path improves the frozen v1 baseline with no material regression in hint adherence, unknown rejection, determinism, memory, or RTF. Thresholds are fitted on development data only and locked before test evaluation.

### M3 — Advanced temporal/overlap path

Probabilistic smoothing, overlap handling, and evidence fusion improve the declared primary metrics while conservative fallbacks are exercised and verified by adversarial tests.

### M4 — Optional neural tier

A safe Rust ECAPA-style embedder implements the common contract, passes weight/feature conformance and public-corpus ablation gates, and remains optional until its accuracy/latency/memory ledger supports promotion.

### M5 — Rollout

Shadow or explicitly requested modes accumulate evidence first. Default changes require an evidence-ledger decision recording exact artifacts, thresholds, rollback triggers, and discrepancies.

## Cross-cutting definition of done

- Each child issue is closed only with named tests and retained evidence, not code inspection alone.
- Every learned or tuned number has provenance and a leakage audit.
- Public evaluation results are reproducible from repository-safe manifests; private local evaluations are reproducible only through opaque local fingerprints and never copy source material into the repo.
- Robot output remains line-oriented, schema-versioned, deterministic where applicable, and free of human decoration.
- All substantive Rust changes pass cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test, and UBS on the changed files, with any unrelated repository-wide debt reported separately rather than hidden.

## Idea-wizard priority map

### Highest-leverage five

1. **Correctness spine — bd-2noc and bd-2noc.1-.3.** Diagnose and repair the native DTW projection contract before treating helper-level accuracy as product proof.
2. **Measurement authority — bd-odj7.10 and bd-odj7.10.2-.7.** Freeze scorer/splits/privacy/oracles/adversarial data, then issue a held-out verdict.
3. **Acoustic representation v2 — bd-odj7.13.1.** Richer voice/channel features, validity masks, quality subwindows, and robust call normalization.
4. **Calibrated probabilistic inference — bd-odj7.13.2, .4, and .5.** Multiscale change posterior, likelihood scoring/count stability, and VB-HMM temporal/unknown decoding.
5. **Optional native neural tier — bd-ohex and bd-ohex.1-.4.** ECAPA conformance, safe Rust inference, shared-contract integration, and independent promotion evidence.

### Next ten complementary bets

6. Enrollment contamination control, profile mixtures, and supervised metric adaptation — bd-odj7.13.3.
7. Explicit overlap detection and dual-speaker attribution — bd-odj7.13.6.
8. Active agent uncertainty queries and reversible contextual enrollment — bd-odj7.13.7.
9. Reversible bounded-memory streaming clustering/correction events — bd-odj7.13.8.
10. Optional multichannel spatial cues — bd-odj7.13.9.
11. Calibrated acoustic/silence/DTW/TinyDiarize fusion — bd-odj7.13.10.
12. Adversarial and metamorphic public-safe condition generation — bd-odj7.10.6.
13. Stage-aware differential external oracles, never runtime dependencies — bd-odj7.10.5.
14. Long-call performance, observability, cancellation, and bounded-memory certification — bd-odj7.13.11.
15. Core and optional integration/promotion matrices plus evidence-led rollout — bd-odj7.13.12-.13 and bd-odj7.11.

## Recommended execution waves

- **Wave 0, parallel:** bd-2noc.1 (DTW diagnosis), bd-odj7.10.2 (scorer/manifest contract), and bd-ohex.1 (optional ECAPA conformance research). Do not start threshold tuning.
- **Wave 1:** bd-2noc.2-.3; bd-odj7.10.3-.6. This yields a correct product path, public splits, privacy guard, diagnostic oracles, and adversarial seeds.
- **Wave 2:** bd-odj7.13.1. Freeze representation ablations on development data.
- **Wave 3, partly parallel:** bd-odj7.13.2, .3, and .4; then .5. The change, enrollment, and cluster scorers share the frozen representation but have separate evidence.
- **Wave 4 core proof:** bd-odj7.13.11, then .12, then bd-odj7.10.7 and the core stages of bd-odj7.11.
- **Wave 4 optional, parallel where safe:** bd-odj7.13.6-.10 and bd-ohex.2-.4; each has independent calibration and fallback.
- **Wave 5:** bd-odj7.13.13 and optional rollout decisions after their named held-out/performance authorities exist.

## First implementation handoff

Start with **bd-odj7.10.2**, which robot triage identifies as the highest-impact unblock, while a separate worker can take **bd-2noc.1**. Claim the exact issue, reserve its narrow files, post progress in the matching Agent Mail thread, and do not close it without the named retained evidence.

title: Acoustic representation v2: richer voice/channel features and robust call normalization
description:
## Outcome

Replace the current eight-dimensional compact speaker vector with a richer, explicitly versioned acoustic representation that separates stable vocal identity evidence from device, distance, codec, and room evidence.

## Background

The current clustering vector retains only six cepstral coefficients, one log-F0 coordinate (zero-filled when unvoiced), and harmonicity. Channel features are separate but globally down-weighted. This is fast and dependency-light, but it discards much of the information needed to distinguish same-gender speakers, muffled far-end playback, microphone proximity, vocal-tract shape, and changing codec conditions. Zero-filling pitch also conflates unvoiced speech with a physical pitch value.

## Work

- Define a versioned FeatureSchema containing dimensions, units, validity masks, normalization rules, and voice-versus-channel ownership.
- Compute richer safe-Rust voice features from existing frames: log-Mel bands or filterbank energies, additional cepstra, deltas/delta-deltas, pitch plus voiced mask and uncertainty, harmonic/noise statistics, spectral slope/tilt, formant-proxy envelope shape, spectral flux, periodicity, and selected temporal modulation summaries.
- Retain a separate channel view: broadband level, noise floor, clipping, spectral rolloff, high-frequency attenuation, codec-like band limitation, reverberation/muffling proxies, and stationary coloration.
- Select high-information voiced subwindows and aggregate them robustly rather than averaging silence, breath, clipping, and uncertain pitch into identity.
- Fit per-recording robust center/scale estimates without allowing a dominant speaker to erase minority-speaker differences; compare global, speech-only, and provisional-cluster normalization.
- Expose deterministic feature diagnostics and missingness without dumping source audio or transcript content.
- Keep the v1 representation available only as an explicit fallback/schema version, not a compatibility wrapper.

## Decisions that must be evidence-driven

Compare representations and subsets by frozen ablation: full vector, no pitch, no channel, no deltas, no modulation features, and v1. Do not assume Fourier or wavelet descriptors help merely because they are available. If wavelet/scattering-style summaries are tested, implement the smallest safe-Rust transform needed and retain them only when held-out evidence justifies latency and complexity.

## Tests

- Unit tests for exact frame counts, finite outputs, silence, impulses, tones, harmonics, chirps, clipped signals, band-limited/muffled speech proxies, short inputs, NaN rejection, voiced/unvoiced transitions, and feature validity masks.
- Property tests for scale invariance where intended, monotonic energy behavior, deterministic output, bounded dimensions, and no panics for arbitrary finite PCM.
- Metamorphic tests showing gain and stationary EQ primarily affect channel coordinates while pitch/formant proxies remain stable within declared tolerance.
- Golden synthetic feature vectors with schema-version checks.
- Public-corpus ablation showing each retained feature family improves a declared metric or calibration outcome without unacceptable RTF/RSS cost.

## Success criteria

- Feature extraction is bounded-memory, deterministic, safe Rust, and versioned.
- On the frozen development protocol, the chosen representation materially improves speaker separability and downstream boundary/attribution metrics over v1.
- On held-out data, it does not regress the primary diarization metric beyond the declared equivalence margin.
- Voice/channel disentanglement tests pass, and missing pitch is never encoded as an ordinary numeric pitch.
- Evidence records schema hash, configuration, scorer version, corpus split fingerprint, RTF, peak RSS, and ablations.

## Fallback

If any new feature is invalid, undersupported, or exceeds its compute budget, mark it missing and use the declared lower-dimensional safe representation. Never synthesize confident identity evidence from missing values.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

## Adaptive representation-selection contract

State is feature validity/quality, voiced coverage, recording-level robust statistics, provisional cluster support, schema version, and compute budget. Actions are use full v2, mask unsupported families, use a reduced declared schema, or fall back to v1. Loss penalizes speaker confusion, channel leakage into identity, missing-evidence overconfidence, latency, and memory. Posterior/confidence is the calibrated feature-quality/support score; calibration is evaluated against downstream held-out separability and reliability, not synthetic signal class alone. The deterministic fallback trigger and selected schema/reason are written to the evidence ledger.

title: Calibrated fusion of acoustic, silence, DTW, and optional TinyDiarize boundaries
description:
## Outcome

Fuse independent boundary evidence through calibrated typed factors so timestamp geometry and optional model signals refine acoustic inference without overriding it through hand-coded snapping.

## Work

- Define a versioned BoundaryEvidence record for acoustic posterior, silence, DTW word/segment geometry, forced hints, and optional TinyDiarize logits.
- Establish independence/correlation assumptions and prevent double-counting evidence derived from the same encoder state.
- Fit a small calibrated fusion model on development data and retain an explicit deterministic rules fallback.
- Use source-specific reliability and missingness; absence of a signal is not negative evidence.
- Produce explanation codes indicating which evidence moved or created a boundary.
- Score each source alone and all declared combinations in ablation.

## Tests

Contradictory evidence, missing sources, invalid timestamps, dense word boundaries, long silence, no silence, TinyDiarize disabled, exact ties, and source reorder. Property tests enforce deterministic commutative behavior where valid, finite probabilities, and typed validation errors.

## Success criteria

- Improves held-out boundary F1/timing error and does not regress DER/JER beyond tolerance.
- Calibration gates pass and evidence ablations support every enabled source.
- DTW-disabled and TinyDiarize-disabled paths remain exact safe fallbacks.
- Robot output exposes provenance without transcript content.

## Fallback

Unsupported schema, invalid geometry, or calibration mismatch selects acoustic-only or the declared deterministic source policy and records the reason.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

## Alien-artifact controller contract

State is the typed set of available boundary sources, source reliability/missingness, dependence group, calibration version, candidate posterior, and compute budget. Actions are accept/move/reject/defer a candidate, choose an evidence subset, or use acoustic/deterministic fallback. The loss matrix prices missed/false boundary, timing error, correlated double-counting, source contract failure, latency, and fallback. The fused posterior is calibrated with Brier/ECE plus boundary precision-recall at declared collars. Invalid geometry, dependence violation, unsupported calibration, or inadequate evidence triggers the deterministic source policy and a ledgered reason.

title: Diarization performance, observability, and long-call certification
description:
## Outcome

Certify that accuracy improvements remain deployable: bounded-memory, deterministic, cancellable, diagnosable, and fast on realistic long recordings.

## Work

- Add stage timers and counters for normalization, framing, feature families, change detection, profile construction, clustering, temporal decoding, overlap, projection, persistence, and correction replay.
- Record peak resident memory and high-water counts for frames, tracklets, prototypes, modes, graph edges, and revisions.
- Define privacy-safe structured diagnostics and stable reason codes for fallback, unknown, rejected hints, invalid geometry, and calibration mismatch.
- Benchmark 10 min, 1 h, and longer generated/public-safe inputs with declared hardware/toolchain/config fingerprints.
- Profile hot paths before optimizing. Evaluate FrankenSciPy/FrankenNumPy components first as differential oracles and only adopt direct dependencies after API, safety, determinism, build, and performance review.
- Vectorize or parallelize only deterministic independent work; preserve cancellation checkpoints and bounded queues.
- Maintain performance/evidence ledger entries for all default-affecting changes.

## Tests

Criterion-style or project-standard microbenchmarks for feature/scoring kernels; long-call integration tests; cancellation at every stage; memory-cap assertions; deterministic repeated runs; log schema tests; disabled-diagnostics overhead checks; malformed input and resource exhaustion.

## Success criteria

- Declared RTF and peak-RSS budgets pass on the certification host with idle/preflight evidence.
- Accuracy mode remains substantially faster than real time or meets the product's declared target.
- No unbounded recording-duration state outside explicitly streamed/spooled artifacts.
- Diagnostics identify stage and fallback cause without exposing source content.
- Optimization changes preserve numeric or byte-exact behavior unless a discrepancy is documented and accuracy-recertified.

## Fallback

If an advanced stage exceeds time/memory budgets, switch at a deterministic checkpoint to the declared lower-cost path and report the degradation; never OOM or silently truncate speaker evidence.

## Runtime fallback controller contract

State includes stage elapsed time, memory/high-water counters, cancellation, remaining budget, enabled modes, and each mode's accuracy-safe fallback eligibility. Actions are continue, disable an optional stage before it mutates authoritative output, switch at a checkpoint to a declared lower-cost path, assign unknown, cancel cleanly, or reject the request. The loss matrix prices OOM, deadline miss, silent truncation, accuracy degradation, lost durability, and fallback. Resource forecasts are calibrated on certification runs and never treated as speaker evidence. Thresholds, chosen action, exact snapshot, and outcome are recorded in the performance/evidence ledger.

title: Core acoustic-v2 integrated test gauntlet and promotion matrix
description:
## Outcome

Provide the integrated proof that the core dependency-light v2 system is correct, more accurate, calibrated, private, deterministic, recoverable, and operational through the real CLI and library surfaces. Core means: DTW projection correctness, measurement authority, feature representation v2, calibrated change detection, enrollment hygiene, probabilistic clustering/count selection, VB-HMM temporal decoding/unknown fallback, and their performance/observability contract. Optional overlap, active-query, streaming-revision, multichannel, fusion experiments, and ECAPA have their own integration matrix and must not block a core acoustic-v2 verdict.

## Coverage matrix

- Unit: every core feature, statistic, constraint, posterior, boundary, profile, scorer, cluster, decoder, projection, serializer, and fallback branch.
- Property: arbitrary finite PCM, time geometry, constraints, speaker permutations, deterministic ties, posterior normalization, bounded state, and no panics.
- Metamorphic: gain, EQ, codec/band-limit, resampling, noise, reverberation, time shift, chunking, and hint subdivision.
- Integration: native engine to DTW words to diarization to segment projection; normalized file path; explicit samples API; contextual hints; cancellation.
- Robot: JSON/NDJSON schema versions, stable error/reason codes, line isolation, deterministic ordering, and no human decoration.
- Persistence: SQLite authority, JSONL export, crash/cancel atomicity, version markers, replay, and documented recovery.
- Evaluation: frozen baselines and ablations for DER/JER, boundary metrics, count, attribution, unknown, hints, calibration, RTF, RSS, and determinism.
- Privacy: repository scan proves no private audio/transcript filename/content or source-identifying metadata; the local private adapter produces aggregate metrics and opaque fingerprints only.
- Adversarial: short turns, same-gender/similar-pitch speakers, far-end muffling, loud near-end voice, channel changes within speaker, interruptions, music/noise, clipping, silence, invalid timestamps, wrong hints, and resource limits.

## Work

- Build a versioned machine-readable matrix mapping each core requirement and known failure to a named test and evidence artifact.
- Add end-to-end fixtures that exercise actual CLI/robot/persistence paths rather than helper-only tests.
- Retain failing seeds and minimized public-safe reproducers.
- Run v1 versus each core ablation with a locked scorer and splits.
