title: Advanced optional-mode integration matrix and independent promotion gates
description:
## Outcome

Integrate and certify the advanced/optional diarization modes after the core acoustic-v2 contract is proven, without delaying the core promotion decision.

## Scope

Overlap-aware dual attribution, active agent uncertainty queries, reversible streaming corrections, optional multichannel spatial cues, calibrated multi-source boundary fusion, and optional ECAPA integration hooks. Each mode remains independently selectable and must preserve the exact core fallback when unavailable or disabled.

## Work and tests

- Create a requirement-to-test matrix for every optional mode and combination that is actually supported.
- Exercise CLI/robot schema negotiation, persistence/recovery, revision events, cancellation, determinism, privacy, performance, and core fallback equivalence.
- Run single-feature and interaction ablations; reject combinations whose correlated evidence double-counts observations.
- Test missing model, mono input, no overlap support, no query authority, streaming resource exhaustion, invalid evidence schema, and calibration mismatch.
- Record operating envelopes and avoid a combinatorial claim beyond tested combinations.

## Success criteria

Every shipped optional mode has named unit/property/metamorphic/e2e tests, retained public held-out evidence appropriate to its claim, and an exact disabled/unavailable fallback. No optional failure corrupts core output or blocks core operation. Promotion decisions and rollback triggers are mode-specific.

## Fallback

Unsupported combinations fail at configuration validation or reduce explicitly to the core acoustic-v2 path with stable reason codes.

title: Fuse ASR context and agent-known intervals as calibrated reversible diarization evidence
description:
## Outcome

Use transcript structure, word timing, discourse/turn-taking cues, and agent-supplied known timestamp intervals to improve boundary, cluster, and speaker-name decisions without allowing language-model plausibility to overwrite contradictory acoustics or manufacture speakers.

## Evidence model

Define typed, versioned factors with explicit provenance and dependence groups:

- acoustic identity and change posteriors;
- word/segment timestamp geometry and silence;
- lexical speaker-change probability near word boundaries;
- conversational adjacency/turn-taking evidence;
- role/name hypotheses from contextual clues;
- hard/soft same-speaker, different-speaker, and named timestamp intervals;
- optional external LLM correction proposal.

Context may propose a boundary, must-link/cannot-link, speaker role/name, or uncertainty query. Every proposal has confidence, scope, source, reversibility, and a rule for acoustic contradiction. Speaker naming is separate from anonymous cluster identity: context may map a stable anonymous profile to a name, but it cannot retroactively create acoustic support.

## Default and optional paths

The built-in dependency-light path uses native ASR words/timestamps and deterministic/local statistical features such as question-answer adjacency, first-person introductions, vocatives, lexical turn probabilities, punctuation, and temporal response patterns. It must work with no network and no external model.

An optional LLM adapter may propose second-pass corrections in a compact schema, inspired by lexical speaker error correction and DiarizationLM. It is never runtime-required, never authoritative by itself, and must be evaluated as a separate mode. Missing, malformed, uncalibrated, privacy-disallowed, or acoustically contradictory proposals are skipped or surfaced for confirmation.

## Known-interval semantics

- Split intervals into quality-scored voiced subwindows before profile learning.
- Hard intervals enforce local attribution but contaminated/low-quality content does not train a profile.
- Soft intervals contribute likelihood according to confidence and acoustic agreement.
- Same/different-speaker relations can span unnamed intervals.
- Contradictions are detected before mutation and returned with stable codes.
- Recompute only the affected dependency cone, emitting deterministic revision and old-to-new label maps.

## State, actions, and loss

State includes acoustic/count/boundary posteriors, ASR timing confidence, contextual factors, constraints, dependency groups, contradiction evidence, profile quality, revision history, and query budget. Actions are accept/downweight/reject a factor, propose/move a boundary, add a reversible relation/name, ask for a timestamp confirmation, preserve anonymous identity, or fall back to acoustic-only.

Loss prices speaker confusion, false contextual correction, missed useful context, name misattribution, privacy leakage, contradiction, label churn, user effort, and latency. Calibrate contextual changes against held-out word-level diarization error and require acoustic-only fallback equivalence when disabled.

## Tests

Unit tests cover question-answer pairs, monologues, backchannels, interruptions, repeated names, self-introductions, ASR errors, missing/invalid word times, wrong soft clues, contaminated hints, overlapping hints, anonymous speakers, contradictory names, no transcript, external adapter failure, deterministic ties, and privacy-safe serialization.

Property/metamorphic tests: disabling context reproduces acoustic output exactly; paraphrase/punctuation changes do not alter identity absent relevant evidence; an untrusted factor cannot override a hard acoustic/interval contradiction; subdividing a known interval preserves the same constraint; accepted revisions are deterministic and reversible.

E2E tests cover library, CLI, robot JSON/NDJSON, SQLite/JSONL, cancellation, crash recovery, query/answer round trips, and word-level speaker attribution. Detailed logs include opaque interval IDs, factor/reason codes, affected stage, prior/posterior deltas, and revision IDs—never transcript text, audio content, private names/paths, or embeddings.

## Evaluation gates

Report DER/JER and boundary metrics plus WDER/cpWER, name-attribution precision/recall, hard-hint adherence, soft-hint gain, contradiction rate, query efficiency, calibration, selective risk, latency, and fallback exactness on public development/held-out data. Freeze the acoustic baseline and contextual calibration before held-out evaluation. Context ships only if it improves attribution without material acoustic, privacy, determinism, or calibration regression.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Refinement pass 2 (context fusion math): group correlated evidence from ASR tokens, punctuation, DTW timing and dialogue heuristics before fusion. Fit source/dependence-group weights on development data with an acoustic-only intercept and conservative shrinkage; absence of a factor is missing data, not negative evidence. Name/role mapping is a separate posterior over stable anonymous profiles and must not feed back as acoustic identity evidence unless a validated interval explicitly authorizes enrollment. Report factor ablations, calibration by source/domain, contradiction rates and counterfactual disabled-output equality.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Refinement pass 5 (agent supervision workflow): extend the existing `speaker-hints-v1` concept through one versioned request/answer schema rather than ad hoc transcript editing. Accept opaque anonymous speaker refs, same-speaker and different-speaker relations, optional name/role mappings, interval policy/confidence, source/dependence group, and query revision ID. A robot response to `speaker_queries` must be replayable, idempotent, bounded, validated before mutation, and return an old-to-new anonymous label map plus affected intervals and revision provenance. The default agent workflow should be: run automatic acoustic inference, inspect only explicit low-confidence/unknown/count queries, submit concise timestamp evidence, and rerun the affected dependency cone. Human CLI help must explain that a name is presentation metadata over an anonymous acoustic profile, not biometric identity. Stable reason codes distinguish rejected geometry, contradiction, contaminated enrollment, unsupported name evidence, stale revision and no acoustic support. Never place transcript text, names, paths, audio, or feature vectors in diagnostics or evidence ledgers.

title: Evaluate bounded wavelet and modulation features as Rust-native diarization sidecars
description:
## Outcome

Determine whether bounded discrete-wavelet, wavelet-scattering-inspired, and modulation-spectrum summaries add real speaker-change or identity information beyond the existing FFT/cepstral/pitch/formant/channel v2 representation. Adopt only evidence-backed, safe-Rust kernels; otherwise retain a documented negative result.

## Motivation and scope

Primary literature reports useful noise-robust speaker-change detection from DWT features and recent unsupervised diarization gains from wavelet scattering plus learned embeddings. This does not establish that wavelets alone identify speakers or that a full scattering network is pragmatic here. Treat these as complementary views, especially for transients, muffling, band limitation, temporal modulation, and multiscale regime changes.

Compare these bounded candidates:

1. Haar and one compact orthogonal DWT over voiced frame envelopes and selected subbands.
2. Multiresolution log-energy, entropy, crest/flatness, and coefficient-change summaries.
3. First/second-order scattering-inspired modulus/average summaries with fixed filters and no learned autoencoder.
4. Modulation-spectrum summaries over cepstral and band-energy trajectories.
5. Existing FFT/cepstral representation as the frozen baseline.

Keep speaker-identity and channel-condition feature ownership explicit. Wavelet channel coloration must not masquerade as identity.

## Engineering contract

- Safe Rust only, bounded levels/windows/state, checked sizes, deterministic coefficient/order semantics, no runtime allocation proportional to recording duration.
- Reuse existing buffers and FFT infrastructure where appropriate.
- FrankenSciPy/FrankenNumPy may serve as local differential oracles for numerical conformance; they are not automatic runtime dependencies.
- Version every adopted feature schema and calibration fingerprint. Default-off until public ablation gates pass.
- Record operation counts, retained bytes, stage timing, and cancellation checkpoints.

## Tests

Golden/differential tests cover impulses, sinusoids, chirps, voiced harmonic proxies, noise, silence, clipping, odd/even lengths, boundary extension, NaN/Inf rejection, and coefficient energy/reconstruction invariants where applicable. Property tests cover bounded finite outputs, deterministic chunking, gain normalization, time shift tolerance, and no panic for arbitrary finite PCM.

Diarization metamorphic tests cover same-speaker gain/EQ/codec/muffling changes, different-speaker similar pitch, abrupt/gradual changes, near/far capture, short turns, and overlap. Detailed diagnostics identify feature family, scale, support, ablation, first divergent stage, and seed without source content.

## Evaluation gates

Run frozen ablations for boundary precision/recall/F1 and timing, same/different pair discrimination, speaker count, DER/JER, calibration, RTF, RSS, and schema determinism on public development and held-out sets. Require improvement beyond predeclared uncertainty with no material channel-confusion or performance regression. If no candidate passes, close with retained negative evidence and do not proliferate features.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Refinement pass 4 (DSP implementation bounds): prototype each candidate as an incremental safe-Rust kernel with fixed maximum levels, declared boundary extension, checked coefficient counts and reusable scratch space; reject parameter sets whose support/window arithmetic overflows or exceeds the request budget. Prefer lifting/filter-bank code only if it preserves the specified normalization and deterministic numerical contract; reuse the existing FFT for modulation spectra where that is cheaper and already audited. Cancellation occurs between independent frames/levels, and incomplete feature families are marked absent rather than filled with zeros. Differential oracle tolerances must be feature/scale specific and retained alongside exact fixtures. Measure incremental RTF/RSS and mutual information or calibrated marginal value before expanding the default vector; no adopted feature may create a new mandatory runtime dependency or ship merely because its isolated boundary score improves.

title: Calibrated multiscale speaker-change posterior and boundary refinement
description:
## Outcome

Replace the fixed Euclidean change threshold and fixed hysteresis with a calibrated, multiscale posterior for speaker regime changes, followed by local boundary refinement.

## Background

The current detector compares left/right means across fixed 100 ms–2 s windows and applies a global threshold. Existing aggregate bootstrap evidence found zero change-point F1 at a 250 ms collar, so threshold tweaking without a scored model would be cargo culting.

## State, actions, and loss

- State: multiscale voice/channel sufficient statistics, speech/voicing quality, silence/DTW/TinyDiarize candidates, local duration, uncertainty, and streaming history.
- Actions: emit no boundary, emit a boundary at a candidate frame, defer for more evidence, or invoke conservative fallback.
- Loss: false split, missed change, timing error, hint contradiction, latency, and fallback cost, with declared weights.
- Output: calibrated change probability, supporting scales, evidence provenance, and refinement offset.

## Work

- Implement variance-aware two-sample/GLR-style distances using robust covariance shrinkage rather than raw global Euclidean distance.
- Compare deterministic CUSUM/Page-Hinkley and bounded Bayesian online change-point approximations; choose by public development evidence, complexity, and streaming suitability.
- Make temporal scales evidence-adaptive while maintaining fixed upper memory bounds.
- Fuse acoustic candidates with silence, DTW token geometry, and optional TinyDiarize only through typed evidence inputs.
- Refine a coarse candidate inside a bounded neighborhood using frame-level posterior, energy minima, voicing discontinuity, spectral flux, and timestamp evidence.
- Calibrate change probabilities with an explicitly fitted map; lock parameters before held-out evaluation.
- Emit stage-specific diagnostics without leaking transcript/audio content.

## Tests

Unit tests cover no-change stationary speech proxies, abrupt speaker changes, gradual channel drift, gain-only changes, silence gaps, short turns, rapid alternation, corrupted timestamps, and end-of-stream. Property tests enforce finite probabilities in [0,1], bounded memory, deterministic ties, monotonic evidence behavior, and fallback on invalid covariance. Metamorphic tests distinguish identity change from gain/EQ/channel-only perturbation. Integration tests score boundary precision/recall/F1 at multiple collars and timing-error quantiles.

## Success criteria

- Substantial improvement over the frozen v1 boundary F1 and timing-error baselines on declared public development and held-out sets.
- Calibration meets declared Brier/ECE gates; reliability diagrams and threshold-selection artifacts are retained.
- No material regression in downstream DER/JER or speaker attribution.
- Streaming latency and memory remain within budget.
- Conservative fallback reproduces a known deterministic mode when posterior estimation is ill-conditioned.

## Fallback

When insufficient voiced evidence, invalid statistics, or calibration mismatch is detected, return an explicit low-confidence/no-decision state and use the fixed safe candidate policy. Do not force a boundary merely to satisfy an expected speaker count.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

title: Enrollment hygiene, profile mixtures, and supervised within-call metric adaptation
description:
## Outcome

Make contextual timestamp hints improve generalization instead of merely enforcing local labels by detecting contaminated intervals, representing speaker modes, and learning only conservative within-call metric adjustments.

## Background

Hard hints now achieve near-perfect adherence, but aggregate held-out attribution fell versus the unhinted baseline. This implies that profile construction or metric adaptation can overfit, absorb another speaker, or overweight channel conditions.

## Work

- Split every enrollment interval into quality-scored voiced subwindows; never treat a whole interval as homogeneous by default.
- Detect contamination through internal multimodality, abrupt change posteriors, poor voiced coverage, outlier distances, and leave-one-subwindow-out consistency.
- Preserve hard constraint semantics for labeled time while separately rating the acoustic interval as usable, partially usable, or unusable for profile training.
- Build multiple bounded modes per speaker for voice state and channel condition, with explicit mode weights and provenance.
- Learn a shrinkage metric or discriminant projection only when the number, quality, and diversity of labeled subwindows support it; otherwise retain the global metric.
- Keep hard and soft hints distinct. Soft hints must contribute probabilistically and be reversible.
- Prevent enrollment leakage across evaluation splits and record all fitted parameter provenance.

## Alien-artifact contract

State includes per-window quality, profile modes, metric covariance, contradiction evidence, and label provenance. Actions are accept, downweight, split, quarantine, or reject a window; update or retain metric; and use global fallback. The loss penalizes contamination, false rejection, hint contradiction, overfitting, and missed adaptation. Confidence is calibrated by held-out enrollment perturbations. Fallback is the immutable global metric plus validated hard constraints.

## Tests

Unit tests cover clean hints, mixed-speaker hints, silence-only hints, wrong soft hints, overlapping hints, one-window enrollment, same speaker under two channels, and two speakers with similar pitch. Leave-one-out and perturbation tests verify that adding low-quality evidence cannot arbitrarily increase confidence. End-to-end tests compare hinted and unhinted accuracy, hint adherence, unknown rejection, and DER/JER.

## Success criteria

- Hinted held-out attribution no longer regresses beyond the declared equivalence margin and should improve on data with useful contextual intervals.
- Hard hint adherence remains at the existing high level, but contaminated hard intervals do not poison out-of-interval profiles.
- Metric adaptation activates only when its support and calibration gates pass, with an evidence record explaining the decision.
- Profile mode count and memory are bounded and deterministic.

## Fallback

If enrollment quality or class support is inadequate, keep the constraints but do not train from the interval; use the global metric and emit a stable diagnostic reason.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

title: Probabilistic speaker scoring, constrained clustering, and stable speaker-count selection
description:
## Outcome

Replace hand-tuned distance and SSE-penalty decisions with calibrated likelihood-ratio scoring, constraint-aware clustering, and stability-based speaker-count selection.

## Background

The current system uses variance-normalized distances with fixed floors, capped agglomeration, and a fixed penalty of SSE plus a constant times K log N. Confidence is derived from a cost margin. Those values have no corpus-bound calibration authority and can be brittle when speakers are acoustically similar or a single speaker has multiple channel modes.

## Work

- Fit a compact diagonal or shrinkage full-covariance same-speaker versus different-speaker likelihood-ratio model on declared development data; compare cosine/whitened distance as the safe baseline.
- Support voice identity and channel condition as separate likelihood components with learned or validated weights.
- Build a constraint graph from hard must-link/cannot-link hints, overlap facts, and contradiction evidence.
- Compare constrained agglomerative clustering with a sparse spectral/co-association formulation; keep complexity bounded by prototype compression and deterministic graph sparsification.
- Estimate speaker count using bootstrap/subwindow stability, eigengap or merge-posterior evidence, and explicit priors/ranges rather than a single fixed penalty.
- Return calibrated assignment/posterior margins and unknown evidence, not a transformed raw distance pretending to be probability.
- Retain a deterministic safe scorer and clustering fallback.

## Tests

Synthetic geometry tests cover well-separated clusters, same-pitch speakers, multi-modal single speakers, minority speakers, identical features, contradictory constraints, one speaker, maximum speakers, and adversarial outliers. Property tests cover permutation invariance, deterministic ties, nonnegative finite costs, must-link/cannot-link enforcement, and bounded prototype memory. Public-corpus ablations freeze the representation while comparing scorers, clustering algorithms, and count selectors.

## Success criteria

- Lower speaker-confusion/DER/JER than v1 on frozen held-out evaluation.
- Speaker-count exact accuracy and absolute-error distributions improve without forcing count when evidence is weak.
- Assignment and unknown confidence meet declared calibration gates.
- Constraints are satisfied or fail closed with explicit contradiction errors.
- Runtime and memory remain within declared budgets.

## Fallback

Ill-conditioned covariance, unstable count selection, graph failure, or calibration mismatch selects the deterministic whitened-distance agglomerative baseline and exposes the fallback trigger in robot evidence.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

## Alien-artifact controller contract

State comprises representation/profile likelihoods, constraint graph, prototype weights, candidate speaker counts, cluster-stability replicates, and calibration versions. Actions are merge, keep separate, assign to a known speaker, assign unknown, choose a supported count/range, or invoke the deterministic baseline. The loss matrix explicitly prices same-speaker splits, different-speaker merges, constraint violations, count error, false known/unknown, runtime, and fallback. Same/different likelihood ratios, count posterior/stability, assignment confidence, Brier/ECE, and selective risk provide posterior/calibration terms. Ill-conditioning, instability, contradiction, unsupported schema, or out-of-domain calibration triggers the deterministic fallback and an evidence-ledger event.

title: Infer a calibrated speaker-count posterior from acoustic evidence without requiring num_speakers
description:
## Outcome

Make automatic speaker-count inference the normal native-acoustic behavior. A caller may omit all count fields and receive an evidence-backed posterior over plausible counts, a selected count only when support is adequate, and an explicit unresolved/unknown-count result otherwise.

`num_speakers`, if retained, must be modeled as a separately typed hard constraint or prior chosen by the caller. It must never silently disable UNKNOWN, force every tracklet into a known label, fabricate occupancy for empty clusters, or turn cardinality alone into `constraints_satisfied=true`.

## Literature-informed design

Use multiple bounded, deterministic views whose failure modes are not identical:

1. Sparse affinity graph over reliable speaker prototypes using calibrated same/different-speaker likelihood ratios.
2. Normalized maximum eigengap or maximum-eigengap analysis over a symmetrized sparse graph as an independent count proposal.
3. Merge-risk/Bayesian evidence accumulated along constrained agglomeration, with an explicit prior over K rather than the current implicit penalty.
4. Jackknife/bootstrap stability across time blocks, feature families, and quality strata.
5. Minimum effective occupancy, voiced-duration support, temporal recurrence, and cluster separation checks for every proposed speaker.
6. Constraint graph lower bounds from non-contradictory hard cannot-links and known-speaker anchors.

Combine these into a normalized posterior or calibrated score distribution over K in `[K_min, K_max]`. Report the full bounded distribution, entropy/stability, evidence provenance, and rejection reason. Do not pretend lane agreement alone is a calibrated posterior.

## State, actions, and loss

State includes candidate K values, sparse affinity/eigenspectrum, merge likelihoods, stability replicates, per-cluster effective occupancy, hard/soft constraint graph, domain/calibration version, and resource budget.

Actions are select K, return a supported range, return count unresolved, request contextual evidence, honor a validated hard count, reject contradictory constraints, or use a declared safe fallback.

The loss matrix separately prices false merge, false split, count error, phantom speakers, collapsed minority speakers, rejected valid evidence, fabricated certainty, constraint violation, runtime, and fallback. False merge and phantom-speaker costs must not be hidden inside one scalar SSE penalty.

## Required semantics

- No count fields: infer K automatically.
- Soft count prior/range: influence the posterior but permit evidence to disagree and report the disagreement.
- Explicit hard count: search only that K, but return unsatisfied/unresolved if minimum evidence and occupancy do not exist; never relabel low-confidence regions merely to cover K labels.
- Known intervals: clean hard anchors establish lower bounds; soft enrollment contributes evidence but not mandatory occupancy.
- UNKNOWN/overlap: remain legal under every count mode.
- `constraints_satisfied`: requires validated hard constraints plus evidence/occupancy gates, not just distinct-label cardinality.

## Tests

Unit tests: one speaker; two/three/five speakers; no speech; identical embeddings; multi-modal single speaker; similar-pitch different speakers; minority speaker; one-frame outlier; channel change without identity change; contradictory anchors; exact K with insufficient evidence; soft prior disagreement; upper-bound saturation; invalid eigenspectrum; deterministic ties.

Property/metamorphic tests: permutation invariance; bounded normalized posterior; finite entropy; chunk/jackknife determinism; gain/EQ/codec/channel perturbations do not create phantom speakers; splitting one homogeneous tracklet does not systematically raise K; adding unsupported K cannot increase `constraints_satisfied`; every selected speaker meets minimum effective occupancy.

Integration/e2e tests through library, CLI, JSON/NDJSON, SQLite/JSONL, cancellation, and recovery must expose the selected mode, posterior/range, evidence fingerprint, per-speaker occupancy, stability, and fallback reason. Logs must be structured, bounded, path-free, and contain no transcript/audio content.

## Evaluation gates

On frozen public development and held-out sets report exact-count accuracy, MAE, count confusion matrix, count NLL/Brier, posterior coverage, calibration/ECE, DER/JER, speaker confusion, dominant-speaker share, minimum-speaker occupancy, and selective risk. Compare fixed penalty, merge-risk, NME spectral, and fused selectors. Predeclare operating points before held-out evaluation.

The candidate may ship only if it improves count reliability without material DER/JER, calibration, determinism, memory, or latency regression. Otherwise remain opt-in and preserve retained negative evidence.

## Rust/dependency contract

Implement safe Rust with bounded sparse matrices and deterministic eigensolver/clustering behavior. Reuse the existing FFT/features and FrankenTorch substrate. FrankenSciPy/FrankenNumPy and external diarizers may be differential test oracles only until build, license, determinism, and performance gates justify a runtime dependency.

title: VB-HMM-style temporal decoding, duration priors, confidence calibration, and unknown fallback
description:
## Outcome

Decode frame/tracklet speaker posteriors with a bounded probabilistic temporal model that respects duration, constraints, overlap eligibility, and uncertainty rather than fixed Viterbi switch penalties.

## Background

The current decoder applies fixed switch penalties and derives confidence from the two best costs. A Bayesian HMM/VBx-style design is a strong first-principles fit for diarization because speaker identity is persistent through time while acoustic observations remain uncertain.

## Work

- Define a compact HMM or variational-Bayes HMM state over speaker profiles plus unknown, with optional overlap handled by a separate gated path.
- Use calibrated acoustic likelihoods from the scoring issue; never double-count hint or channel evidence.
- Learn or robustly estimate duration/transition priors on development data, with explicit caps for short turns and streaming latency.
- Incorporate hard/soft constraints through typed potentials whose provenance remains visible.
- Produce smoothed posterior probabilities, calibrated confidence, and a reasoned unknown decision.
- Measure Brier score, ECE, reliability by confidence bin, unknown precision/recall, and selective-risk curves.
- Define deterministic update order and bounded-memory forward/backward or fixed-lag smoothing.

## Alien-artifact contract

State: current speaker posterior, duration, profile reliability, observation likelihoods, constraint potentials, overlap eligibility, and calibration version. Actions: assign a known speaker, assign unknown, defer within lag, or fall back. Loss includes confusion, false unknown, false certainty, excessive switching, hint contradiction, and latency. Fallback uses the existing deterministic constrained decoder with locked safe parameters.

## Tests

Unit tests cover one speaker, rapid alternation, long turns, short turns, missing observations, contradictory hints, low-confidence profiles, end-of-stream flushing, and fixed-lag equivalence. Property tests enforce posterior normalization, deterministic output, bounded lag/memory, no illegal transitions, and graceful invalid-likelihood fallback. E2E tests compare raw cluster assignments versus temporal decoding through CLI/robot/persistence.

## Success criteria

- Improves held-out DER/JER or speaker-confusion without harming boundary timing beyond tolerance.
- Confidence/unknown calibration passes declared gates and selective risk decreases as low-confidence output is rejected.
- Fixed-lag streaming and offline decoding agree within a documented bound.
- Every adaptive parameter and fallback decision is evidence-ledgered.

## Fallback

Any invalid likelihood, posterior collapse, unsupported calibration version, or excessive uncertainty switches to explicit unknown or the deterministic safe decoder; it never silently emits a high-confidence label.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

title: Add profile-conditioned frame activity and iterative overlap-aware resegmentation
description:
## Outcome

After initial clustering produces provisional profiles and a count posterior, rescore the recording frame-by-frame for each supported speaker and iteratively refine boundaries, UNKNOWN, and overlap. This adapts the central TS-VAD/VBx insight to a bounded Rust-native core without requiring a heavyweight neural runtime.

## Design

- Build a calibrated per-frame/per-tracklet activity likelihood for each profile from voice identity, channel-conditioned reliability, voicing quality, change posterior, and optional embedding evidence.
- Keep identity likelihood separate from speech activity and channel fit; prevent loudness, distance, or stationary EQ from becoming permanent identity.
- Decode a factorial or powerset-bounded temporal state: silence, one known speaker, UNKNOWN, and at most supported two-speaker overlap states.
- Apply semi-Markov/VB-HMM-style duration priors and fixed-lag or offline smoothing. Transition probabilities must not be fixed magic penalties.
- Re-estimate profiles only from high-posterior, non-overlapped, quality-qualified frames. Use bounded iterations, convergence checks, reversible sufficient statistics, and rollback to the previous authoritative iteration.
- Condition on known intervals as typed potentials. Hard intervals control attribution locally; soft intervals influence profile likelihood according to confidence and enrollment quality.
- Preserve an exact deterministic baseline and explicit no-improvement/invalid-posterior fallback.

## State, actions, loss, calibration

State includes speaker profiles/modes, count posterior, frame likelihoods, duration state, overlap eligibility, UNKNOWN, constraints, iteration history, and resource budget. Actions are assign one speaker, assign overlap pair, assign UNKNOWN/silence, move a boundary, update/quarantine a profile mode, stop, or roll back.

Loss separately prices confusion, false/missed overlap, false known, false UNKNOWN, boundary error, profile contamination, oscillation, latency, and fallback. Calibrate speaker activity, overlap, and UNKNOWN probabilities separately; evaluate selective risk and iteration-to-iteration reliability.

## Tests

Unit/property tests cover one speaker, rapid alternation, long/short turns, dominant/minority imbalance, near/far and muffled/clear channels, same-pitch speakers, within-speaker channel changes, overlap, silence, missing likelihoods, invalid covariance, contradictory hints, convergence, oscillation, cancellation, deterministic ties, posterior normalization, and bounded memory/iterations.

Metamorphic tests require label stability under gain/EQ/codec changes, chunk/fixed-lag consistency, and no new speaker from tracklet subdivision. E2E tests exercise CLI/robot/persistence/recovery, revision provenance, and detailed path-free diagnostics.

## Success gates

Against frozen initial clustering, the refinement must improve or remain within predeclared equivalence margins for DER/JER, speaker confusion, overlap F1, boundary timing, UNKNOWN precision/recall, calibration, RTF, RSS, and count stability. Any failed gate retains the previous iteration/output and logs the rollback reason.

comments.text: Refinement pass 2 (temporal mathematics): specify emissions as calibrated log likelihoods and constraints as separately provenance-tagged log potentials; never add the same channel/hint evidence twice through profile and transition terms. Use log-sum-exp forward/backward with normalized finite posteriors, explicit duration distributions and deterministic truncation. Iterative updates require a monotone penalized internal objective, collapse/occupancy guards, maximum iterations, and rollback to the last valid snapshot; internal monotonicity is not an accuracy claim, so held-out DER/JER/calibration still control promotion. Test label-permutation invariance, posterior mass conservation, zero/one likelihood boundaries, extreme-duration priors and fixed-lag approximation error.

comments.text: Refinement pass 4 (bounded temporal inference): construct the allowed state set only from supported profiles and admissible overlap pairs, with explicit caps on speakers, pairs, duration bins, iterations and fixed-lag history. Complexity and retained memory must be stated for offline and streaming modes before implementation; do not materialize a full recording-by-speaker posterior table when a bounded forward/backward window or spooled artifact suffices. Reuse reversible sufficient statistics and preallocated frame/profile buffers. Put cancellation and resource checkpoints before every profile update and temporal sweep; cancellation returns the last complete authoritative iteration, never a half-updated profile. Validate all dimensions and log potentials, use deterministic summation/tie breaking, and make convergence/rollback O(bounded state) rather than cloning unbounded audio-derived state. If supported speaker count makes powerset or pairwise overlap decoding exceed budget, fall back at a declared checkpoint to single-speaker-plus-UNKNOWN decoding and report the capability reduction.

It does not cluster, create/delete/rename speakers, update profiles, run ECAPA again, change segment or tracklet timestamps, or claim frame-level TS-VAD/overlap/profile learning. Boundaries may move only at existing tracklet edges.

Integration point: after canonical labels, incumbent Viterbi, evaluate_speaker_evidence, and retain_supported_assignments; before final speaker count, constraint, and profile finalization. The supported profile set and count posterior are immutable.

State and actions: for T tracklets, states are the fixed supported profiles plus UNKNOWN. A transition may keep a supported label, map UNKNOWN to a supported label, change between supported labels, or emit UNKNOWN. Hard-hint and overlap rows are forced states inside one global DP, not split block boundaries. Only the incumbent primary state is finite on forced rows; after acceptance the complete incumbent assignment structure for forced rows, including primary, secondary, confidences, and flags, must remain bit-exact.

Objective: reuse the existing profile/cluster emission terms, apply soft priors exactly once, apply ECAPA duration evidence exactly once, and apply channel evidence only where already authorized. Recompute UNKNOWN against supported competitors. Local rejection is represented in the emission lattice before decoding. All arithmetic is finite fixed-order f64. Commit only when candidate_total.total_cmp(&incumbent_total).is_lt(); an exact tie preserves the incumbent. Internal objective improvement is not an accuracy claim.

Budgets and cancellation: T <= 2048, supported K <= 8, total states S <= 9, emission evaluations <= 16,384, transitions <= 165,807, local score visits <= 147,456, backpointers <= 18,432, staged states <= 2048, exactly one redecode, zero profile updates, zero model calls, explicit scratch <= 131,072 bytes, cancellation polling at least every 32 scored blocks. Any cap, non-finite value, cancellation, replay mismatch, or validation failure returns the original incumbent bit-for-bit.

Validation and rollback: stage only speaker IDs and confidences. Before commit validate exact timeline/index identity, exact hard-hint and overlap-row identity, every non-UNKNOWN label in the frozen supported set, unchanged supported set/count posterior, exact constraints, strict objective improvement, and deterministic structural replay. Disabled mode must not enter the helper. Evaluation evidence is feature-free and separate from production output. No environment/default enablement is authorized.

Frozen paired public-dev gate: both arms consume one prepared observation, incumbent partition, and profile set; order is balanced; candidate replay and path-free evidence are mandatory. Require exact common input/count/hash/supported-label/hint/overlap topology and zero new inference. Enforce the budgets above. Promotion requires strict aggregate micro DER and speaker-confusion improvement, macro DER and macro JER non-regression both combined and per engine, change-F1/boundary-MAE/selective-risk/coverage/calibration non-regression with at least one strict target gain, no one-speaker regression, no per-recording speaker-count or DER regression, partition RTF overhead <= 25 percent, total RTF <= 1, peak RSS <= 512 MiB, and scratch <= 128 KiB. A loss remains negative dev evidence only; the gate must not be weakened or rewritten after results are seen.

title: Overlap detection and overlap-aware dual-speaker attribution
description:
## Outcome

Represent and score overlapping speech explicitly so that two active speakers can be attributed when evidence supports it instead of forcing every instant into a single-speaker state.

## Work

- Define overlap as a first-class interval type with primary/secondary speaker posterior, confidence, provenance, and projection semantics.
- Build a dependency-light overlap detector from harmonic competition, multi-pitch evidence, modulation/spectral residuals, and inconsistency between single-speaker profile likelihood and speech confidence.
- Calibrate the detector on licensed public overlap references; do not promote from synthetic mixtures alone.
- Gate dual assignment using the top speaker posteriors and temporal context, with conservative thresholds and an explicit unknown-secondary option.
- Specify CLI JSON/NDJSON and SQLite/JSONL schema behavior, including versioning and consumers that do not request overlap.
- Ensure DER/JER scoring can report both overlap-aware and collar/non-overlap variants.

## Tests

Synthetic mixtures cover unequal levels, same/different pitch, music/noise impostors, silence, and clipping. Public-reference tests measure overlap precision/recall/F1 and overlap-aware DER. Projection tests cover word and segment boundaries crossing overlap intervals, zero supported secondary evidence, serialization/recovery, and deterministic ordering.

## Success criteria

- Improves overlap-aware held-out metrics without unacceptable false-overlap regression on non-overlap speech.
- Schema is stable, typed, and robot-safe.
- The single-speaker fallback remains exact when overlap support or calibration is unavailable.
- Compute and memory remain within budget.

## Fallback

If overlap probability, secondary attribution, or time geometry is uncertain, emit a single primary speaker plus explicit overlap uncertainty; never fabricate a second known speaker.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

## Alien-artifact controller contract

State includes speech confidence, overlap feature validity, overlap posterior, primary/secondary speaker posteriors, temporal context, calibration version, and projection support. Actions are single known speaker, primary known plus secondary known, primary plus unknown secondary, defer, or core fallback. The loss matrix prices missed overlap, false overlap, wrong secondary identity, fabricated certainty, latency, and fallback. Calibrate overlap and secondary-attribution probabilities separately with Brier/ECE and precision-recall operating points. Weak/unsupported evidence deterministically selects single-speaker core output and records the reason/evidence fingerprint.

title: Active agent uncertainty queries and reversible contextual enrollment
description:
## Outcome

Let an AI agent ask for the smallest high-value timestamp confirmations, then rebuild affected speaker profiles and assignments deterministically without rerunning unrelated work.

## Work

- Rank candidate intervals by expected reduction in speaker uncertainty, profile ambiguity, boundary ambiguity, and count uncertainty.
- Emit robot-safe query objects containing opaque interval IDs, times, uncertainty reason codes, candidate equivalence groups, and expected information gain; never include transcript text unless a separate authorized consumer adds it.
- Accept answers as versioned hard/soft same-speaker, different-speaker, or speaker-name constraints with provenance and confidence.
- Recompute only the dependency cone affected by an answer while producing a deterministic revision event and old-to-new speaker-label map.
- Detect contradictory answers before mutating profiles.
- Define query budgets, cooldowns, and no-query fallback.

## Tests

Tests cover ambiguous pairs, redundant queries, contradictory answers, query budget exhaustion, deterministic ranking, no speech, one speaker, privacy-safe serialization, persistence/recovery, and incremental-versus-full recomputation equivalence.

## Success criteria

- On simulation and public annotated calls, a small fixed query budget improves attribution/count metrics over no-query baseline.
- Queries are stable under deterministic replay and contain no source content.
- Contradictions fail closed with stable robot error codes.
- Incremental rebuild matches full recomputation within exact or declared numeric tolerance.

## Fallback

When information-gain calibration is absent or all candidates are low value, emit no query and preserve the current diarization result.

## Alien-artifact controller contract

State includes interval uncertainty, profile/count/boundary entropy, expected information gain, existing constraints, query budget/cooldown, and answer provenance. Actions are query one interval/relation, defer, stop querying, apply a validated answer, reject a contradiction, or rebuild through full fallback. The loss matrix prices user/agent effort, redundant questions, incorrect confident answers, label churn, unresolved diarization error, and recomputation cost. Expected gain and post-answer accuracy/calibration are scored on held-out simulations. Low gain, unsupported calibration, exhausted budget, or contradiction triggers deterministic no-query/preserve-result fallback and an evidence event.

Full answer ingestion, contradiction-aware dependency-cone recomputation, persistence, and public quality proof remain outstanding behind blocked prerequisites, so the issue stays open.

title: Reversible bounded-memory streaming speaker clustering and correction events
description:
## Outcome

Support long-running and live audio with bounded-memory speaker profiles, fixed-lag assignments, reversible merges, and explicit correction events.

## Work

- Define streaming state, prototype eviction/compression, fixed-lag boundary/label decisions, and monotonic revision IDs.
- Make profile merges reversible through a bounded provenance ledger or sufficient statistics that permit split/rebuild within a declared horizon.
- Emit schema-versioned add/update/retract speaker-turn events suitable for JSONL consumers.
- Reconcile late contextual hints and agent answers without rewriting already consumed output invisibly.
- Define deterministic eviction, tie-breaking, and speaker-label continuity.
- Integrate cancellation checkpoints and ensure no partially persisted revision becomes authoritative.

## Tests

Long synthetic streams, many speakers, speaker return after long gaps, profile drift, late hints, merge-then-split, cancellation at each persistence boundary, restart/recovery, fixed-memory assertions, and offline-versus-streaming comparison.

## Success criteria

- Peak memory is bounded independently of recording duration for declared speaker/prototype limits.
- Streaming output converges toward offline output within declared lag and quality bounds.
- Every changed past label is represented by a correction event.
- Deterministic replay produces byte-equivalent event sequences.
- Crash/cancel recovery preserves a valid authoritative prefix.

## Fallback

When revision state is exhausted or evidence is too weak, freeze committed history, use unknown for new ambiguous regions, and emit a stable degradation reason rather than performing an irreversible speculative merge.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

## Alien-artifact controller contract

State includes fixed-lag posteriors, profile sufficient statistics, merge/split provenance, revision horizon, memory high-water marks, and committed-output authority. Actions are emit provisional, commit, merge, split, retract/update, evict/compress, assign unknown, or freeze history. The loss matrix prices identity error, late churn, irreversible wrong merge, memory/latency, correction volume, and data loss. Confidence is calibrated against offline agreement and revision correctness; memory pressure is a separate resource posterior, not identity evidence. Horizon/resource exhaustion, invalid provenance, cancellation, or posterior collapse triggers freeze-plus-unknown fallback and a ledgered correction/degradation event.

title: Optional multichannel spatial-cue sidecar for stereo and call recordings
description:
## Outcome

Exploit stereo/multichannel spatial information when present while leaving mono behavior unchanged and dependency-light.

## Work

- Preserve channel layout through normalization when explicitly requested; default mono ASR normalization must remain available.
- Compute bounded inter-channel level, delay/phase, and coherence summaries at speech frames.
- Treat spatial cues as a separate optional observation view, never as permanent identity.
- Calibrate channel-swap invariance and microphone-layout uncertainty.
- Fuse cues only when channel count, coherence, and calibration version qualify.
- Extend robot diagnostics and evidence manifests without exposing raw audio.

## Tests

Synthetic stereo delay/level fixtures, channel swap, collapsed mono, decorrelated noise, reverberant mixtures, missing channels, and resampling. Verify mono byte-equivalent fallback and deterministic spatial summaries.

## Success criteria

- Improves declared stereo-call development/held-out metrics when spatial separation exists.
- No regression or schema break for mono inputs.
- Invalid layouts and weak coherence cause explicit fallback.
- Memory/latency budgets are met.

## Fallback

Collapse to the canonical mono acoustic path whenever layout, coherence, or calibration support is insufficient.

## Cross-cutting engineering gates

Any new diagnostic, log, or evidence output must be structured, bounded, schema-aware, and privacy-safe: no transcript text, audio excerpts, private filenames, per-recording identities, or embeddings may be retained in repository artifacts. If this work changes a public library type, CLI flag, robot event, JSON/NDJSON field, SQLite row, or JSONL record, update every consumer and add version/round-trip/error-code tests in the same change. Record stage, configuration/schema version, fallback reason, and calibration/evidence fingerprint so failures are attributable without exposing source content.

## Alien-artifact controller contract

State includes channel count/layout, delay/level/coherence evidence, spatial calibration version, mono acoustic posterior, and signal quality. Actions are fuse spatial evidence, ignore one or more cues, collapse to mono, or report unsupported. The loss matrix prices speaker confusion, channel-layout overfit, mono regression, latency, and fallback. Cue reliability and fused confidence are calibrated on held-out multichannel conditions, including channel swaps. Unknown layout, weak coherence, calibration mismatch, or mono input deterministically selects byte-equivalent mono fallback and records the reason.

title: Add typed diarization request, hint, turn, profile-summary, and report models
description:
BACKGROUND
The live model has only SpeakerConstraints, an external-backend-oriented DiarizationConfig, one optional segment speaker string, and one confidence field that means ASR confidence.

SCOPE
Introduce typed public library models for acoustic engine selection, known speaker intervals, hard and soft hint policy, opaque speaker references, diarized turns, independent speaker confidence, change confidence, overlap suspicion, profile quality summaries, algorithm and feature schema identities, fallback status, and a complete DiarizationReport attached to TranscriptionResult. Preserve ASR confidence as a distinct field.

VALIDATION
Reject non-finite, negative, reversed, or out-of-range intervals; confidence outside 0..1; empty references; contradictory overlapping hard hints; inconsistent exact/min/max speaker constraints. Give every failure a stable machine-readable code. Raw voice vectors are not part of normal serialization.

COMPATIBILITY
Early development permits direct schema correction instead of compatibility shims. Update constructors and fixtures deliberately.

## Acceptance Criteria

All new public types serialize deterministically; invalid hints and constraints fail with stable error codes; ASR confidence and speaker confidence are distinct; hard and soft policy semantics are documented and unit-tested; raw biometric feature vectors are absent from default JSON; all existing call sites are updated without compatibility wrappers.

## Public User Contract

Known intervals are supplied as schema speaker-hints-v1 with speaker_ref, start_ms, end_ms, confidence, policy, and optional provenance. speaker_ref is an opaque within-run reference, not a legal identity claim. HardMustLink and SoftEnrollment are serialized snake_case. The top-level request selects Acoustic, External, Neural, or Auto and carries explicit fallback policy. DiarizationReport is optional when diarization is not requested and always names implementation and feature schema when present.
acceptance_criteria: All new public types serialize deterministically; invalid hints and constraints fail with stable error codes; ASR confidence and speaker confidence are distinct; hard and soft policy semantics are documented and unit-tested; raw biometric feature vectors are absent from default JSON; all existing call sites are updated without compatibility wrappers.

title: Factor fixed-frame spectrum and implement bounded acoustic feature extraction
description:
BACKGROUND
The native Whisper mel frontend already owns a tuned deterministic 400-sample FFT at 16 kHz with a 160-sample hop. Whisper global log-mel normalization removes amplitude and channel evidence needed by diarization.

SCOPE
Expose or factor a crate-private fixed-frame one-sided power-spectrum primitive without changing Whisper log-mel numerical output. Build a streaming acoustic feature extractor over 25 ms frames and 10 ms hops. Maintain separate voice and channel views. Voice features include non-globally-normalized cepstral envelope, deltas, YIN-like F0 with voicing confidence, harmonicity, and voiced fraction. Channel features include RMS and dynamics, centroid, bandwidth, rolloff, flatness, spectral tilt, band ratios, crest/clipping, noise-floor, and conservative smearing/distortion proxies. Every frame includes a quality mask.

RESOURCE CONTRACT
Do not retain raw whole-call frame matrices. Aggregate incrementally. Cancellation must be checked at bounded frame intervals. fsci-fft, fsci-signal, and fsci-cluster begin as dev oracles; production dependencies require matched evidence. The ASR mel path must remain byte-identical.

## Acceptance Criteria

Feature extraction reads real PCM and distinguishes designed low/high pitch and clear/muffled/gain fixtures; voice and channel feature groups are explicit; F0 failure yields unvoiced rather than fabricated pitch; non-finite inputs fail safely; cancellation is bounded; long-input peak memory is bounded by streaming state; differential tests cover spectra/descriptors; existing Whisper mel golden bytes remain unchanged.

## Initial Bounded Defaults

Use exactly 16,000 Hz, 400 samples per frame, and 160 samples per hop for acoustic-v1. Check cancellation at least every 32 frames. Reuse fixed scratch buffers and aggregate frames into robust microturn statistics as soon as boundaries permit. Any feature dimension, epsilon, pitch range, or quality threshold is part of feature-schema-v1 and must appear in replay evidence; no hidden environment-only behavior lever may default on.

## Audio Source Contract

Feature extraction consumes the canonical normalized 16 kHz mono WAV used by ASR, bound by normalized_input_sha256. Existing NativeAudioAnalysis energy regions may seed quality and VAD state but cannot substitute for samples. Future multichannel sidecars are explicitly out of acoustic-v1 and must not change mono replay semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Feature extraction reads real PCM and distinguishes designed low/high pitch and clear/muffled/gain fixtures; voice and channel feature groups are explicit; F0 failure yields unvoiced rather than fabricated pitch; non-finite inputs fail safely; cancellation is bounded; long-input peak memory is bounded by streaming state; differential tests cover spectra/descriptors; existing Whisper mel golden bytes remain unchanged.

title: Implement multiscale acoustic change detection and speaker-homogeneous tracklets
description:
BACKGROUND
ASR segments can contain multiple speakers. Speaker segmentation must happen before speaker clustering and must use acoustic changes rather than text length or temporal position.

SCOPE
Compute robust left/right distribution distances on selected feature trajectories. Add inexpensive Haar-like contrasts at multiple scales near 100 ms, 250 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, and 2 s. Fuse local maxima with VAD regions, silence gaps, optional TinyDiarize turn tokens, and DTW word boundaries. Apply hysteresis, boundary guards, minimum speech evidence, and minimum turn duration. Produce conservative microturns and sequentially merge strongly compatible adjacent microturns into tracklets.

HONESTY
Wavelets are a multiscale step detector, not a claim of speaker identity. Overlap-like energy/harmonic anomalies are marked as overlap-suspected, not force-labeled.

## Acceptance Criteria

Synthetic step, silence, gradual drift, noise burst, no-change, short-turn, and cancellation tests pass; detected turns are finite, ordered, bounded, and deterministic across thread counts; change-point scores include component evidence; VAD and word boundaries are fused without making text a speaker feature; no full raw-audio CWT or unbounded frame retention is used.

## Segmentation Complexity

Compute multiscale contrasts over bounded rolling windows rather than storing a full CWT. Candidate boundaries are deduplicated with deterministic earliest-index tie breaks. Retain only compact per-microturn sufficient statistics and the output timeline. The algorithm is linear in frames apart from bounded local window work.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic step, silence, gradual drift, noise burst, no-change, short-turn, and cancellation tests pass; detected turns are finite, ordered, bounded, and deterministic across thread counts; change-point scores include component evidence; VAD and word boundaries are fused without making text a speaker feature; no full raw-audio CWT or unbounded frame retention is used.

title: Implement known-interval validation, enrollment, and robust speaker profiles
description:
BACKGROUND
Agents need to supply recording intervals they infer belong to the same speaker. Those intervals must improve within-run profiles without silently poisoning the entire call.

SCOPE
Validate KnownSpeakerInterval values against exact normalized-audio sample bounds. Hash the canonical hint document and retain confidence and provenance. Remove configurable edge guards, intersect with speech and frame-quality masks, and accumulate robust median, MAD, quantile, count, voiced-duration, and reliability statistics. Same speaker_ref creates must-link or soft-enrollment evidence by policy. Distinct hard references are cannot-link. Soft evidence contributes bounded pseudo-counts and priors and can be rejected as contradictory. Permit multiple channel subprofiles under one voice identity.

PRIVACY
Profiles are within-run and ephemeral by default. Default events/persistence contain summaries and hashes, never raw vectors or audio.

## Acceptance Criteria

Hard intervals are immutable; contradictory hard hints fail closed; soft hints can be downweighted or rejected with evidence; edge guards and speech-quality filtering are tested; multiple intervals for one reference merge deterministically; one speaker can retain multiple channel subprofiles; profile serialization defaults to non-biometric summaries; hint document hashes are replay-stable.

## Hint Failure And Poisoning Policy

Hard hints with different speaker_ref values may not overlap after sample quantization. Hard intervals with one reference are immutable but still exclude non-speech and boundary guards from enrollment; if no usable voiced evidence remains, validation fails instead of producing an empty trusted profile. Soft enrollment has capped pseudo-count weight, records contradiction score, and may be ignored. An untrusted provenance string is metadata only and cannot increase confidence.

title: Implement scalable constrained clustering, temporal smoothing, and unknown rejection
description:
BACKGROUND
The current greedy fixed-threshold cosine clusterer is order-sensitive and uses incompatible mixed features. Dense all-pairs clustering over every microturn is not acceptable for multi-hour calls.

SCOPE
Use robust variance-normalized voice likelihood as the primary distance and capped channel distance as secondary within-call evidence. Compress adjacent microturns into tracklets and bounded sufficient-statistic prototypes. Run deterministic constrained agglomeration on the capped prototype set, honoring hard must-link/cannot-link and exact/min/max speaker counts. Infer count with a penalized likelihood or BIC-style objective plus stability diagnostics. Refine labels across all microturns with a Viterbi-style temporal pass and switch penalty.

CONFIDENCE
Compute best-versus-second assignment margin, profile reliability, bootstrap stability, and calibration status. Emit UNKNOWN on insufficient or ambiguous evidence. Canonicalize anchored labels first, then unanchored profiles by earliest reliable occurrence and stable hash tie-break.

## Acceptance Criteria

Hard constraints are never violated; soft hints influence but do not force assignments; exact/min/max counts behave consistently; output is deterministic across input-equivalent ordering and thread count; ambiguous and short evidence becomes unknown; multi-hour synthetic inputs stay within documented prototype and memory caps; tests cover false-merge, false-split, channel-change, speaker-return, and stable-label cases.

## Clustering Complexity

Set a versioned default cap of 512 global prototypes per run for acoustic-v1, configurable through typed policy. Before the cap, merge only the closest compatible low-radius prototype using deterministic ordering; never discard anchored prototypes. Exact constrained agglomeration is O(P squared) in capped prototype count P, followed by O(M times K) smoothing across M microturns and K speakers. Report cap pressure and fallback rather than silently degrading.

title: Project diarized turns onto DTW word boundaries and attributed transcript segments
description:
BACKGROUND
A single Whisper segment may contain a real speaker change. Assigning one label to the entire segment hides that change or falsely attributes words.

SCOPE
Keep an independent diarized-turn timeline. When DTW word timings exist, intersect turns with words and split transcript segments only at legal word boundaries. Preserve text order and bytes. When word timing is absent, assign a speaker only if one profile dominates the segment duration with sufficient confidence; otherwise emit mixed_speaker_segment and unknown. Preserve overlap-suspected evidence. Rebuild transcript text through existing canonical helpers.

INVARIANTS
Turns and projected segments are finite, monotonic, deterministic, within audio bounds, and never invent text. Speaker confidence remains independent of ASR confidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

Mid-segment speaker changes split at DTW word boundaries without text loss, duplication, or reordering; boundary ties have deterministic rules; no-word-timing mixed segments remain honestly unknown; one-speaker segments retain ASR confidence unchanged; overlap suspicion survives projection; unit and end-to-end fixtures cover returns to a prior speaker and changes near segment edges.

## Projection Ownership

DiarizedTurn remains the acoustic source of truth. TranscriptionSegment speaker fields are a convenience projection for existing renderers. Projection must not mutate the acoustic turn timeline or treat punctuation boundaries as acoustic evidence. If one word overlaps a change boundary, use maximum timed overlap, then earlier speaker as deterministic tie-break only when confidence is above policy; otherwise mark the word unknown.

title: Centralize acoustic diarization pipeline ownership and expose CLI and robot controls
description:
BACKGROUND
Native whisper-diarization currently runs the heuristic internally while the generic Diarize stage may also run. Stage skip decisions use the requested backend rather than the resolved backend, making Auto ownership ambiguous.

SCOPE

title: transcribe: --offset-ms and --duration-ms silently ignored by native backend
description:
## Summary

`fw transcribe --offset-ms` and `--duration-ms` are accepted by the CLI but have **no
effect** on the native whisper.cpp backend. The whole file is transcribed either way.
There is no warning, no error, and no field in the JSON saying the flags were dropped —
so a caller that uses them to probe a region silently pays full-file cost and gets
full-file output.

## Reproduction (v0.7.2, darwin_arm64, `--backend whisper-cpp`)

Make a 120 s clip, then:

```
$ fw transcribe --input dur_test.wav --backend whisper-cpp --no-diarize --no-persist \
    --language en --duration-ms 20000 --json | jq '.result.segments[-1].end_sec'
119.99            # expected: ~20

$ fw transcribe --input dur_test.wav --backend whisper-cpp --no-diarize --no-persist \
    --language en --offset-ms 60000 --json | jq '.result.segments[0].start_sec'
0.0               # expected: ~60
```

Both flags are documented in `fw transcribe --help` as "(whisper.cpp)", which is exactly
the backend in use (`result.backend == "whisper.cpp-native"`).

## Why it matters

Region probing is the standard way an agent inspects an unfamiliar recording cheaply —
checking whether a suspect stretch is speech, music, or silence before committing to a
full run. With these flags inert, a 20 s probe costs a full-file decode. In this
session a "70 s probe" of a 45-minute file took 6 minutes, because it decoded all 45
minutes. That silently inverts the cost model agents plan around.

## Suggested fix

Honor both flags in the native backend by slicing the normalized PCM before decode, and
offset the emitted timestamps by `offset_ms` so they stay in the source timebase.

If a backend genuinely cannot support a passed flag, that must be **loud**: either fail
with a usage error, or record it in `result.warnings` / a
`request.ignored_options` array so `--json` consumers can see it. A silently-dropped
option is the worst of the three outcomes.

## Acceptance

- `--duration-ms N` produces segments ending at ~N ms.
- `--offset-ms N` produces segments starting at ~N ms, in source-file time.
- Wall-clock scales with the requested slice, not the file.
- Any option a backend cannot honor appears in a machine-readable ignored/warning field.
close_reason: Fixed: whisper.cpp-native slices normalized PCM by --offset-ms/--duration-ms before decode (wall-clock scales with slice), shifts all emitted timestamps (segments, DTW word timings, window stats, dropped windows) back into source timebase, records raw_output.audio_window provenance, skips the whole-file silence pre-gate on windowed runs, returns clean empty result for offset past EOF. Backends that cannot honor the window now push a machine-readable RunReport.warnings entry and are listed in robot backends unsupported_options; diarize+window runs warn that diarization covers the full clip. Unit tests for bounds/shift/flag plumbing added.

title: Optional Rust-native ECAPA-TDNN embeddings behind the common diarizer contract
description:
## Outcome

Implement an optional memory-safe Rust-native ECAPA-TDNN speaker embedding provider behind the common acoustic diarization contract, without creating a second segmentation/clustering/output stack and without making learned weights required for native diarization.

## Architectural role

The dependency-light acoustic v2 path owns speech/change tracklets, contextual constraints, profile/clustering/temporal contracts, projection, schemas, persistence, privacy, evidence, and fallback. ECAPA supplies a versioned SpeakerRepresentation view for suitable voiced tracklets. It may augment or replace the classical voice embedding only when its calibration and runtime gates pass. Channel/environment evidence remains separate.

## Work

- Specify the exact training/export family, weight license/provenance, tensor names/shapes/dtypes, feature frontend, normalization, frame handling, minimum voiced duration, embedding normalization, and expected numerical tolerances.
- Implement 80-bin Kaldi-style filterbanks (25 ms/10 ms, without Whisper utterance-global normalization), folded BatchNorm inference, SE-Res2/TDNN blocks, multi-layer aggregation, channel-dependent attentive statistics pooling, and 192-dimensional embeddings using safe Rust plus audited FrankenTorch kernels.
- Cache only by normalized input hash, weights hash, feature schema, algorithm version, tracklet sample range, and calibration version; persistence remains default-off.
- Plug into the common representation/profile/scoring contracts and reuse hints, constraints, unknown, temporal smoothing, overlap, DTW projection, robot schemas, SQLite/JSONL, cancellation, and rollout policy.
- Make model absence, invalid weights, unsupported CPU/backend, too-short speech, or resource limit a typed unavailable/degraded outcome.
- Compare ECAPA-only, classical-only, and calibrated fusion through the same frozen scorer.

## Tests

- Frontend conformance against the authoritative exporter/reference on tones and public-safe speech.
- Tensor shape, BatchNorm folding, Res2 block, attention weight normalization, pooling, embedding norm, malformed weights, and deterministic inference.
- End-to-end real-weight same/different speaker discrimination, diarization DER/JER, overlap/count/hints/unknown/calibration, cancellation, persistence/replay, RTF/RSS, and cross-backend tolerance.
- No test based only on synthetic pitch separation may certify real-speaker accuracy.

## Success criteria

- Common contract integration has no independent ASR-segment clustering or output path.
- Real licensed weights and public held-out data establish improvement or a clearly bounded optional niche.
- Accuracy, calibration, latency, memory, determinism, cancellation, and privacy gates pass with retained evidence.
- Missing/invalid model falls back honestly to the calibrated classical acoustic path or reports unavailable; it never invokes or labels the lexical heuristic as acoustic/neural.
- Default behavior remains gated until the rollout ledger explicitly authorizes a change.

## Non-goals

No Python runtime, no vendored diarization framework, no secret/unlicensed weights, no ECAPA-specific schema fork, and no promotion based on external benchmark claims alone.
acceptance_criteria: ECAPA implements the common bd-odj7 diarizer contract; no independent ASR-segment cluster/output path remains in the bead; real-weight corpus evidence covers DER/JER, verification discrimination, calibration, hints, cancellation, replay, memory, and RTF; model absence falls back honestly to calibrated acoustic-v1 or unavailable, never the lexical heuristic; default behavior remains gated until retained rollout evidence exists.

title: Certify ECAPA public-corpus accuracy, calibration, performance, and rollout evidence
description:
## Outcome

Decide from frozen public evidence whether ECAPA should remain experimental, be an opt-in accuracy tier, or enter a broader rollout stage.

## Work

Predeclare gates; run classical-only, ECAPA-only, and calibrated fusion on frozen development/held-out corpora; report DER/JER, change/count/overlap, hint behavior, unknown/selective risk, Brier/ECE, domain slices, RTF/RSS, cache effects, cancellation, and deterministic replay. Analyze training-domain mismatch and weight-license/distribution constraints. Record an evidence-ledger decision and rollback triggers.

## Success criteria

No promotion without statistically supported held-out value and passing runtime/privacy gates. If gains are narrow, document the supported operating envelope. Model absence must retain classical behavior. Synthetic-only and external published numbers cannot close the issue.

title: Pipeline Enhancement: Advanced Multi-Stage ASR Processing
description:
EPIC: Pipeline Enhancement

The current pipeline has 5 stages: ingest → normalize → backend → accelerate → persist. This is a good start but misses several powerful capabilities from the legacy systems.

New stages to add (inspired by whisper-diarization's multi-stage approach):
1. VAD Pre-filtering: Voice Activity Detection to identify speech segments before sending to ASR. Dramatically reduces processing time for audio with lots of silence/noise. Inspired by whisper.cpp's Silero-VAD integration.
2. Source Separation: Isolate vocals from background noise/music (Demucs-inspired). Improves speaker embedding accuracy and ASR quality on noisy audio.
3. Forced Alignment: CTC-based timestamp correction after initial ASR. Whisper's timestamps can drift at segment boundaries; forced alignment uses emission probabilities to find true boundaries. Critical for accurate word-level speaker mapping.
4. Speaker Diarization: TitaNet-inspired speaker embedding + clustering. Identify who said what. Currently delegated entirely to backends; bringing this in-house gives more control.
5. Punctuation Restoration: Multilingual punctuation model (12+ languages). The diarization pipeline strips punctuation during alignment; restoration makes transcripts readable.

Pipeline should also support:
- Skip/include stages based on request (e.g., skip diarization if not needed)
- Stage-level caching (don't re-normalize if already WAV)
- Parallel stage execution where possible (e.g., VAD + source separation)
- Progress reporting per stage (for robot mode and TUI)

Each new stage must follow the existing EventLog pattern — emit stage start/complete events with payloads for observability.

Key architectural decision: New stages should be composable and optional, not monolithic. The pipeline configuration should be declarative.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pipeline includes all stages: ingest, normalize, VAD, source separation, backend, alignment, diarization, punctuation, accelerate, persist
- Stages are composable and independently testable
- Each stage emits robot events
- Pipeline handles errors at any stage with proper cleanup
- All pipeline tests pass.

Stages are composable and independently testable. Each stage emits robot events. Pipeline handles errors at any stage with proper cleanup. All pipeline tests pass.

description:
Forced alignment corrects ASR timestamp drift using CTC emission probabilities. Whisper's timestamps can drift 0.5-2 seconds at segment boundaries; forced alignment finds the true word boundaries.

Inspiration: whisper-diarization uses ctc-forced-aligner.

Why this matters: Word-level speaker attribution requires precise word boundaries. Without forced alignment, speaker boundaries will be wrong.

2. POST-BACKEND STAGE: Runs AFTER backend produces initial transcript. Takes transcript text + original audio → produces aligned word timestamps. These replace the backend's less-accurate timestamps.

- Works with output from any backend

- Stage emits robot event with alignment statistics.
